text:
🔥 3 AI investment stories that made me rethink where the real money is going.

Everyone is chasing AI chips, data centers and the next big winner.

But some of the most interesting opportunities are hiding one layer beneath the headlines.

Three stories caught my attention.

1. Marvell: The AI story isn't just about chips. It's about moving data.

Marvell is targeting $70B–$90B in revenue by 2031, compared with roughly $8.2B today.

Sounds almost unbelievable.

But here's what I find interesting: a huge part of the thesis rests on optical interconnects and high-speed data transmission.

You can build the most powerful AI chip in the world. If thousands of chips can't communicate efficiently, the entire system hits a bottleneck.

That's where Marvell comes in.

Custom AI chips offer another growth opportunity, but interconnect could be the foundation of the story.

The risk? Technology changes quickly, and custom silicon is a competitive business with a concentrated customer base.

I'm more interested in whether Marvell can turn this demand into operating profits than in the headline $80B target.

2. Google and nuclear power: Time may be worth more than money.

AI companies are running into a problem that money alone can't solve overnight: electricity.

Google's reported $4.3B agreement with Constellation Energy is aimed at upgrading existing nuclear capacity.

Think about that for a moment.

Building a new nuclear plant can take many years. Upgrading an existing facility with the right infrastructure and approvals may bring additional power online much sooner.

When AI infrastructure is expanding rapidly, waiting 10–15 years isn't an attractive option.

This changes the investment equation for nuclear power.

The opportunity isn't just owning a nuclear plant. It's owning a plant that can generate more electricity, sooner, under long-term contracts.

Of course, not every reactor can be upgraded, and execution still matters.

But the market may be starting to value something it previously overlooked: the ability to deliver reliable power when everyone else is waiting for it.

3. SpaceX: A partner today, a competitor tomorrow.

This might be the most fascinating story of the three.

SpaceX has reportedly agreed to an approximately $8B spectrum transaction that could help Starlink Mobile expand into direct mobile services.

For years, satellite connectivity has complemented traditional telecom networks, filling coverage gaps where cell towers struggle.

Now imagine that same partner deciding it wants the customer, the monthly subscription and the pricing power.

That's a very different relationship.

AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile have spent decades building networks and acquiring spectrum. SpaceX already has rockets, satellites and an established global infrastructure.

It doesn't need to build everything from scratch.

But satellites aren't magic. Spectrum capacity, indoor coverage, ground infrastructure and regulatory approvals remain real constraints.

The real question is whether SpaceX can use its existing infrastructure to enter mobile communications at a lower incremental cost than traditional operators.

If it can, the threat goes beyond losing subscribers.

It could put pressure on the pricing power that has made telecom such a profitable business.

And that's why the market is paying attention.

The bigger picture?

These three stories look unrelated at first.

One is about semiconductors. Another is about nuclear energy. The third is about telecommunications.

But I see a common thread.

AI is creating demand for infrastructure that most people barely think about: moving data, generating electricity and connecting users.

The biggest winners won't necessarily be the companies with the loudest AI narratives.

They may be the companies that remove the bottlenecks everyone else eventually has to pay for.

That's where I'd spend more time looking.

Because in an infrastructure boom, the most valuable business isn't always the one everyone is talking about.

Sometimes, it's the one everyone else depends on.

PowerCompute's September update is out, and the balance sheet is barely recognizable from where it was three months ago.

The company mined 8.1 BTC in September, up 37% from last year — and pulled in roughly $89,000 just by selling power back to the grid during heat-driven curtailment at its Oklahoma and Mississippi sites. That curtailment income brought Q3 energy sales to about $312,000.

But the real line item is on the balance sheet: PowerCompute applied 267.4 BTC to fully repay its $22.45 million Arch credit facility, cutting total secured debt from $23.7 million to $1.25 million. Holdings dropped from 323 BTC to 63.7 — every coin went to retire debt, not to market sales.

CEO Bruce Rodgers was blunt about it: "We used Bitcoin to retire debt rather than carry leverage." And in the hottest months, he says, selling megawatts back to the grid pays more than mining on them — so the company will keep directing each megawatt to whichever use offers the best risk-adjusted return, whether that's mining, energy sales, or eventually HPC.

That's the small miner's version of the playbook in one quote: power as the asset, Bitcoin as working capital, debt optional.

text:
Stopped in traffic on I-44 in Oklahoma City.
A pickup hits me from behind.
We pull onto the shoulder.
Me: "Can I see your insurance card?"
Driver: "I don't have insurance."
Me: "None?"
Driver: "It lapsed. I'm sorry."
My neck already hurts.
I call the police, then my own insurance company.
Adjuster: "Let me check whether you have uninsured motorist coverage on your policy."

Here is what most people do not realize about that question.
Under 36 O.S. § 3636, an Oklahoma auto liability policy generally can't be issued without uninsured motorist coverage.
The way out is a rejection in writing by the named insured or applicant.
The offer has to come on a written form, separate from the application.
That form lists four choices.
One of them reads: "I want to reject Uninsured Motorist coverage."

The statute says the coverage is for bodily injury.
The form names three drivers it covers:
→ An uninsured motorist.
→ A hit-and-run motorist.
→ Or an insured driver without enough liability insurance to pay for your injuries.
The minimum on the form is $25,000 per person and $50,000 per occurrence.
A rejection you signed years ago generally stays valid for the life of the policy.
P.S. Look up 36 O.S. § 3636 and read the form yourself.

“Southern Brazilian hair” — cabelo brasileiro do sul — is a premium category in the human-hair trade. Suppliers source ponytails from people in southern Brazil, selecting them for extensions, wigs and hairpieces sold both locally and abroad.

The category is associated with the South’s white, European-descended communities. Its reputation centres on fine, silky strands and naturally lighter colours. That describes selected hair entering the trade, rather than everyone living in the region.

The selection includes brunettes, dark blondes and lighter blondes, with straight or naturally wavy textures. For someone with fine hair, matching the thickness and movement of their own strands can matter as much as getting the colour right.

Naturally blonde, virgin hair is especially prized: the colour grew that way, without dye or bleach. Suppliers assess length, weight, strand thickness, chemical history and the condition of the ends. Each ponytail is a different piece of material.

The prices are substantial. Brazilian retailer A Rainha dos Cabelos lists Southern Brazilian blonde hair at R$2,250–2,520 per 100g before its Pix discount. At those rates, 200g costs R$4,500–5,040, before fitting. These are retail prices, not payments to donors.

The international connection is concrete. Goldylost’s founder travels to Curitiba to select ponytails personally. The brand sells wigs and toppers through boutiques in Sydney and Miami, and markets virgin European and Southern Brazilian hair in its luxury range.

• Pix is Brazil’s instant payment system. A “Pix discount” is a lower price offered when you pay through it.

text:
The permanent cuts in the One Big Beautiful Bill are the TCJA rates (10% to 37%), the higher standard deduction, and the child tax credit. Those hit the middle class, not just the top bracket. The temporary pieces are the new tips, overtime, and senior deductions. Calling the rate structure a gift only to the rich is the opposite of what the law did. Without it, rates were set to snap back higher for almost everyone in 2026.​

US refineries have been running at roughly 90-98% utilization. Operable capacity is about 18.2 million barrels a day, near the recent peak and higher than the early 1980s even after plant closures. The country exports crude and products because shale production and complex Gulf Coast refineries produce more than domestic demand in some grades and products. That is not unused capacity sitting idle for 40 years. It is a market.​

The 1990-91 recession ended in March 1991. Clinton took office in January 1993 into a recovery that was already underway, even if the job market was still soft. Reagan’s expansion after the Volcker recession was real: strong real growth and roughly 16 million jobs. Debt rose with defense spending and interest costs. That is not the same as inventing the 1990s. The tech boom and later surplus also had a Republican Congress after 1994 and a private-sector internet, not a presidential rescue from a plot to ban access. Clinton signed the Communications Decency Act himself.​

Healthcare costs are driven by third-party payment, regulation, administration, and liability. Private equity is a recent layer, not the original cause. Medical bills are a factor in some bankruptcies. They are not the sole number-one driver in the way the talking point claims. Republicans have offered market reforms and HSAs for decades. They have not pretended a government takeover was the only option.

The scoreboard still does not turn into “Republican philosophy fails 90% of the time” once the oil shocks, Fed timing, and rebound bookkeeping are counted. A 10-year lease and a multiyear defense contract still do not reset on Inauguration Day. That is not an excuse. It is how the economy actually works.

text:
I’ve worked in technology for years, but I’ve also tried fish farming twice.

Failed both times, unfortunately. 😂

And yet, I wouldn’t describe those experiences as a complete waste. I learned lessons about business, money, planning, and decision-making that I probably wouldn’t have learned the same way sitting behind a computer.

Which is why I find our obsession with pushing everyone into tech a little strange. Everywhere you turn, someone is telling young people to learn coding, become a data analyst, get into cybersecurity, or find something to do in AI.

And don’t get me wrong. Those are all interesting fields with real opportunities. But must everyone work in tech?

There are people who could build remarkable businesses in agriculture, manufacturing, and other industries, but who are busy chasing technology careers simply because that’s what everyone says they should do. @omoalhajaabiola says a lot of good stuff along those lines and is always sharing opportunities!

Sometimes, I wonder how many people are struggling to build careers in technology, not necessarily because they have any particular interest in it, but because they’ve been made to believe that’s where all the money is.

There’s money to be made outside tech too. Of course, none of it is guaranteed. But, sometimes, the opportunity you’re looking for isn’t in the industry everyone is talking about.

We need to encourage young people to explore opportunities based on their interests, abilities, resources, and the problems they can genuinely solve, rather than simply following whatever industry happens to be fashionable.

There’s nothing wrong with pursuing a career in tech. But there’s also nothing wrong with becoming a farmer, a manufacturer, or building a business around something that has absolutely nothing to do with software.

And if you’re so enamored by technology, there’s a lot of value you can offer by bringing tech into those spaces.

Enough said!

Old & New Perspectives On Paul
Helpful Thread of Quotes Etc. from the book:
Perspectives Old and New on Paul
The "Lutheran" Paul and His Critics
—by STEPHEN WESTERHOLM

Thread by @ DrawNear_ 

Begin Thread:

“For Paul, sin at its root is something far more egregious than the violation of rules; it represents the rejecting and insulting of a person—indeed of the very One to whom humans owe everything they are and have and who himself wills their own well-being.”

On Romans 2:
“Paul allows that human beings (even Gentiles!) may do good, yet declares all humankind to be culpable before God. His point is not that no one ever does things that are right, but rather that all people do things that are wrong.”

“The message of Rom 3… is not that mercy triumphs over judgment, but that, in a world gone awry, divine goodness has reasserted itself, granting drastic recognition to the reality of sin, yet restoring God’s sinful creatures to their intended place of glory in God’s creation.”

“The required human response is that of ‘faith.’ …note that the required response does nothing, in Paul’s mind, to jeopardize the nature of divine redemption as a gift granted freely to sinners by the grace of God.”

“Love of a person is neither oblivious nor indifferent to the unique nature of the person loved. Still, love is impossible without an object, and the nature of love’s object colors the nature of love.”

The same is true of faith: One trusts someone (or something) one has found, or has reason to believe, trustworthy. In requiring an object, then, trust is like love: it, too, is elicited, experienced, and expressed in ways dependent on its object.
True trust is a response elicited by the trustworthiness or goodness of the one trusted; and the strength and character of true trust inevitably depend on our perception of the character of the one we trust.
What God has done in Christ has been (among other things) to furnish a fresh and prodigious demonstration that he is worthy of human trust. The natural, appropriate response evoked by the proclamation of the Christian message should thus be faith, or trust, in God: faith is awakened by hearing the word of Christ.

Paul can speak as though “faith” began with the coming of Christ, a claim that seems consistent with the view that humanity, apart from Christ, is in a state of rebellion against God.
Abraham, like the Christian, was declared righteous, not because he had done what is right, but because he responded with faith to an initiative of God’s grace.

“Without faith, it is impossible to please God.”
“Whatever is not an expression of faith is sin.”
“Deeds cannot be either God-pleasing or good when they represent behavior adopted by a self that, at its deepest roots, is determined to pursue its own goals.”
—Stephen Westerholm

“For Paul, the belief that God has acted on our behalf in Christ awakens a proper trust in God: ‘We are those who trust in [God], who raised Jesus our Lord from the dead, who was handed over for our transgressions and raised so that we might be declared righteous.’ Appropriate faith in God thus follows from the conviction that the Christian message of what he has done is true.”
“1 Peter 1:21 provides a good summary of the point: ‘By Christ you believe in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God.’”
“God’s demonstration of his trustworthiness in Christ is thus the means, not merely of atoning for human sins, but also of spurring rebellious humans to a living faith in God.”

“Paul can speak as though ‘faith’ began with the coming of Christ, a claim that seems consistent with a view that humanity, apart from Christ, is in a state of rebellion against God. On the other hand, he does allow Abraham as a model of Christian faith: a common pattern is seen in that Abraham, like the Christian, was declared righteous, not because he had done what was right, but because he responded with faith to an initiative of God’s grace.”

“The Psalmist of the Bible found joy in the presence of God: an overwhelming sense that, wherever one found oneself, and whatever one’s circumstances, God is there—and God is good. The joy may be expressed, as the Psalms frequently enjoin, with music and dance and boisterous shouts. It may find voice in a quiet prayer of assurance: ‘When I awake, I am still with thee.’ In any case, the Psalmists repeatedly speak of discovering in the Eternal, not only their provision and protection, but also their heart’s delight.”

“Not incidental to the pleasure was the belief that the enjoyment was mutual: ‘He [God] delighteth not in the strength of the horse: he taketh not pleasure in the legs of a man. The LORD taketh his pleasure in them that fear him, in those that hope in his mercy.’”

“For his part, Paul believes that a spirit of rebellion has infected all humankind, and done so with disastrous effect; but also that God has reasserted his tzedakah [the goodness of God seen in his faithfulness toward his creation], provided atonement for the ravages of sin, and in the process summoned humanity to return to the embrace of his goodness. To trust the God who has demonstrated his love in Christ is to be ‘reconciled’ to him to be ‘at peace’ with him and restored to his good graces and at the same time to be assured of a share in God’s eternal glory: cause enough, Paul declares, for exuberant celebration.”

No academic discussion can convey the experience of persistent joy that comes from being grounded in the divine favor.

In the eternal relationship between the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit is proof that God is eternally a God of love: even before there were creatures for God to love, the Father loved the Son; the Son loved the Father; both loved and were loved by the Holy Spirit.
“Romans 5:10 is not concerned with the details of Christian doctrine. The point is rather that Christians can be sure of the bliss God has promised when they remember the length to which God was prepared to go to make it possible.”

[Screenshot Text]
10 For if when we were enemies we were reconciled to God through the death of His Son, much more, having been reconciled, we shall be saved by His life.
[End Screenshot Text]

Like birds with broken wings, human beings who refuse to accept their place in God’s world are no longer free to enjoy life as it was meant to be lived. From their disastrous enslavement to the lie of their own independence, the self-absorbed need to be set free.

[Screenshot Text]
of their living a life defined (in part at least) by sin.
Yet, however rooted in human nature sin may be, it cannot be natural and still be sin. Sin is, necessarily, a distortion of what ought to be, and Paul believes that people remain aware, at some level, of the wrongfulness of much of what they do, and desire, at some level, to do better. In this sense there is within human beings an “I” that recognizes goodness and longs to embrace it. Yet such is the hold of sin upon people’s lives that they cannot yield the truly good more than fitful acknowledgment. They are sin’s slaves—paradoxically, both with their will (they choose to do what they should not do) and without it (they nonetheless recognize and regret the wrong in what they do). So Paul depicts the disordered personality of Adamic humanity.¹²
12In this paragraph I have drawn on Romans 7:15–24. Some interpreters, however, think that this passage has in view the continued moral struggles of the Christian. They think it unlikely that Paul would attribute to Adamic humanity a desire for what is good. I (with many other interpreters) find it more improbable that Paul could depict Christian existence as one of being “sold under sin” (Romans 7:14; contrast Romans 6:18, 22), powerless to deal with the “flesh” (Romans 7:18; contrast Romans 8:9), engaged in a struggle with sin in which God’s Spirit plays no evident part (note the absence of any reference to God’s Spirit in 7:15–24; and contrast Romans 8:3–4, 9). See further chapter 9, below.
[End Screenshot Text]

“People do much that would be both good and God pleasing if it were done as an expression of their wholehearted faith in God… ‘Whatever is not an expression of faith is sin.’”

[God is pleased by wholehearted faith in Himself, no matter who expresses it.]
Westerholm’s expansion on Paul’s principle of “the wages of sin is death.”

[Screenshot Text]
1Humans were made to enjoy a privileged position in a world created good.
2Through their refusal to acknowledge and trust God, and their determination to pursue their own (self-defined) good, humans have fallen from the “glory” for which God intended them.³⁹
3Such was the choice of Adam. His sin marked out the boundaries within which humanity now lives. People choose, commit, and are responsible for their own individual sins. In so doing, however, they are merely giving personal expression to the will for self-rule that characterizes the whole human race.
4Humans retain enough of a sense of the good to know that they have sinned against it, and indeed desire, at some level, to do what is right. Their sin thus remains a sin against the truth, a living lie that destroys the sinner’s integrity.
5Sin kills.
[End Screenshot Text]

[Jesus] was sent as God’s Son to condemn & conquer sin. This accounts for his ability (not otherwise found in humanity) to overcome sin and live a life marked by radical trust and obedience toward God: Such—it must be remembered—was the life for which all humanity was intended.
The life and death of Christ as a man, and the possibility he procured for humanity to be delivered from sin and restored to God’s favor, are all gifts of God’s grace. Paul does not begrudge the ink required to underline the point. (Rom 5:15-21)

God refuses to abandon his creatures to the power of evil. His purpose is to rescue humanity through Christ. To accomplish this end, he has ordained that Adamic human beings can be “united with Christ.”

Their baptism marks them out as those who, with Jesus, have died to the life that was marred by sin and now share with Christ a new life in God’s service. The baptized are no longer “Adam people,” but by divine transference, “Christ people…”
Those who, with Christ, have “died to sin” have been set free from its tyranny. While they clung to their self-rule and self-absorption, they could not lose themselves in God’s love, embrace and delight in his goodness, or know the sense of belonging in a Cosmos stirred by his benevolence.
Becoming like Christ is a transformation taking place over a lifetime. But would-be believers cannot reembrace the lie of their own independence or give themselves to the pursuit of sin without losing the freedom they now claim to enjoy.
To understand Paul, we need to recapture the vision of a cosmos fashioned and steered by divine goodness, with human beings a vital part of its order.

Paul on the distinction between God’s universal moral law and ceremonial Jewish laws, laws which were to give the Jews the opportunity to obey and trust God in all areas of their lives.

[Screenshot Text]
Though all of torah’s commands were “righteous” and “good,” their righteousness and goodness were of different kinds.¹⁰ Paul does not draw explicit distinctions in his writings. Nonetheless, when he speaks of Gentiles who keep the law, or of the law’s requirements as “written” on Gentile “hearts” and attested by their “conscience,”¹¹ he is clearly referring to the moral demands of the Mosaic law: Gentiles, too, know that it is wrong to murder, commit adultery, steal. It is clear that Paul did not think that Gentiles were aware of, or subject to, an obligation to keep Israel’s food or festival laws. The same exclusive focus on the law’s moral demands may well be present when Paul says that Christians are enabled by God’s Spirit to fulfill “the righteous demand of the law,”¹² and that “love is the fulfilling of the law.”¹³ The moral demands of the law are “righteous” and “good” because they spell out what behavior is appropriate for all human beings living in God’s world.

But the law also contains commands about circumcision, festival observances, and permitted and forbidden foods: Paul insisted that these commands were not to be imposed on Gentiles even when Gentiles become members (together with Jewish Christians) in the new people of God. The righteousness and goodness of such demands¹⁴ lay in the opportunity they gave Jews to trust and obey God in all areas of their lives. These commands, however, were given only to Jews. In Paul’s view (shared by many Jews), it was neither in their nature nor in God’s purpose that they should be universalized.
[End Screenshot Text]

“Salvation was to be found in Christ who had died for the sins of humanity… Paul sums up the gospel that he himself received and that he had preached to others: ‘Christ died for our sins…’”

One would expect the God of all the earth to open a path to fellowship with himself that puts all peoples on an equal footing. Such is the path, not of the law, but of faith…
Paul notes in Romans 3:27 that while boasting is invited by a law that demands “works,” it is excluded if the pathway to divine favor is that of faith.

[Screenshot Text]
stating the truth about humans and their place in God’s world that is not affected by their response.⁴⁰
But it is also (Paul would say) good that the law identified sin as such and condemned it. Sin was present in the world and worked its deadly bane throughout the period from Adam to Moses, even before the law was given:⁴¹ murder, adultery, and theft did not first become wrong when God included them in the list of things that Israel was not supposed to do. But the giving of the law served to mark out such sins as transgressions: as the willful violation of identifiable, recognized, and legitimate demands.⁴² Deeds wrong in any case now represented the deliberate flouting of God’s commands.⁴³ Indeed (as noted earlier in this chapter), when the rebellious “flesh” encountered God’s law, its inchoate rebelliousness acquired a focus against which it could direct its defiance, and sin multiplied.⁴⁴ Not that the spread of sin is a good thing; but the recognition⁴⁵ and indictment⁴⁶ of humanity’s rebelliousness are good, even necessary steps in the ultimate banishment of all that corrupts the goodness of God’s creation.⁴⁷
[Romans 3:19–20 NRSV inset:]
Now we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced, and the whole world may be held accountable to God. For “no human being will be justified in his sight” by deeds prescribed by the law, for through the law comes the knowledge of sin.
[End Screenshot Text]

In giving the law, God provided his wayward creatures with a fitting and graphic reminder that he is good, that human beings have been made to enjoy fellowship with him, and that that fellowship requires their own submission to the good.

Where I to trust divine goodness as I ought, I would not be tempted to lie, to cheat, to cover it, to steal, to hurt, to become jealous, or bitter.
“Such is the divine salvation offered in Paul’s gospel…”

Nonetheless, when he speaks of Gentiles who keep the law, or of the law’s requirements as “written” on Gentile “hearts” and attested by their “conscience,”¹¹ he is clearly referring to the moral demands of the Mosaic law: Gentiles, too, know that it is wrong to murder, commit adultery, steal. It is clear that Paul did not think that Gentiles were aware of, or subject to, an obligation to keep Israel’s food or festival laws. The same exclusive focus on the law’s moral demands may well be present when Paul says that Christians are enabled by God’s Spirit to fulfill “the righteous demand of the law,”¹² and that “love is the fulfilling of the law.”¹³ The moral demands of the law are “righteous” and “good” because they spell out what behavior is appropriate for all human beings living in God’s world.

But the law also contains commands about circumcision, festival observances, and permitted and forbidden foods: Paul insisted that these commands were not to be imposed on Gentiles even when Gentiles become members (together with Jewish Christians) in the new people of God. The righteousness and goodness of such demands¹⁴ lay in the opportunity they gave Jews to trust and obey God in all areas of their lives. These commands, however, were given only to Jews. In Paul’s view (shared by many Jews), it was neither in their nature nor in God’s purpose that they should be universalized.
[End Screenshot Text]

“Salvation was to be found in Christ who had died for the sins of humanity… Paul sums up the gospel that he himself received and that he had preached to others: ‘Christ died for our sins…’”

One would expect the God of all the earth to open a path to fellowship with himself that puts all peoples on an equal footing. Such is the path, not of the law, but of faith…
Paul notes in Romans 3:27 that while boasting is invited by a law that demands “works,” it is excluded if the pathway to divine favor is that of faith.

[Screenshot Text]
stating the truth about humans and their place in God’s world that is not affected by their response.⁴⁰
But it is also (Paul would say) good that the law identified sin as such and condemned it. Sin was present in the world and worked its deadly bane throughout the period from Adam to Moses, even before the law was given:⁴¹ murder, adultery, and theft did not first become wrong when God included them in the list of things that Israel was not supposed to do. But the giving of the law served to mark out such sins as transgressions: as the willful violation of identifiable, recognized, and legitimate demands.⁴² Deeds wrong in any case now represented the deliberate flouting of God’s commands.⁴³ Indeed (as noted earlier in this chapter), when the rebellious “flesh” encountered God’s law, its inchoate rebelliousness acquired a focus against which it could direct its defiance, and sin multiplied.⁴⁴ Not that the spread of sin is a good thing; but the recognition⁴⁵ and indictment⁴⁶ of humanity’s rebelliousness are good, even necessary steps in the ultimate banishment of all that corrupts the goodness of God’s creation.⁴⁷
[Romans 3:19–20 NRSV inset:]
Now we know that whatever the law says, it speaks to those who are under the law, so that every mouth may be silenced, and the whole world may be held accountable to God. For “no human being will be justified in his sight” by deeds prescribed by the law, for through the law comes the knowledge of sin.
[End Screenshot Text]

In giving the law, God provided his wayward creatures with a fitting and graphic reminder that he is good, that human beings have been made to enjoy fellowship with him, and that that fellowship requires their own submission to the good.

Where I to trust divine goodness as I ought, I would not be tempted to lie, to cheat, to cover it, to steal, to hurt, to become jealous, or bitter.
“Such is the divine salvation offered in Paul’s gospel…”

WOH, Episode 10. Summary 43. A few more reflections on the ghosts of Ghost Valley. WKX continues his game with the ghosts, realizing that his plan has succeeded. He has terrified most of them, and Changing Ghost is in such a state that he will have to think twice before acting against the Master of Ghost Valley. For now, WKX asks who killed the Master of the Tai Shan Sect; he turns to Happy Ghost, noting that marks left on the victim's face point to him. Happy Ghost moves his hands away from his face, revealing a ghastly smile formed by scars on his cheeks. He begins to laugh, explaining that it wasn't him—he was framed. LQQ watches him closely, while Changing Ghost is so focused that he stares blankly ahead. Chuckling, Happy Ghost insists it wasn't him, claiming he wouldn't deny it if it were. Kneeling beside him, Lovelace surely wonders if WKX will find something against him, too. WKX asks if Happy Ghost finds the situation amusing. Lovelace glances at WKX, wondering if his companion will become the next victim. Happy Ghost explains to WKX that his behavior and appearance are due to a long-standing affliction. LFM looks as though she wants to say something but merely glances around; Happy Ghost clarifies that he has breathing difficulties, which force him to laugh whenever he speaks. Hearing this explanation, WKX begins to laugh as well, and Happy Ghost begs for mercy. Deep down, he is undoubtedly anxious, having witnessed the fate of the White Grim Reaper—who had also pleaded with WKX for forgiveness. Ghost cannot be certain how WKX will react or whether he might lose his life in the process. WKX laughs, remarking on the humor of the situation, and Happy Ghost—realizing that the best way to avoid provoking him is to hide one’s face—does exactly that. WKX declares that their terrified expressions are highly amusing. He then gets down to business, explaining the need to find something else equally entertaining. He cites the upcoming Heroes' Conference—which he dismisses as a gathering of sanctimonious scoundrels—as an example, noting it is scheduled for two days hence. He invites them to offer their own proposals, insisting they devise a cunning plan to utterly shatter the pride of those three curs from the Five Lakes Alliance, ensuring they can never form an alliance again. He concludes by noting just how amusing that will be. WKX’s final speech catches the ghosts off guard; they had not expected him to back down and forgo seeking another victim. Changing Ghost realizes that WKX is not to be trifled with; he has received a warning, as have the other members of the Ten Devils. He understands that even as the leader of a small group of ghosts, he cannot conspire against WKX, who could easily discover such a plot. The spectacle of the White Grim Reaper’s punishment was merely a glimpse of what WKX is capable of. It seems the ghosts had forgotten how WKX became the Leader of Ghost Valley. Now, the realization hits them: their Leader is a madman who is currently restraining himself, but if they cross a certain line, things could end very badly for them. Through his behavior, WKX showed them that there is no room for weakness or submission in Ghost Valley. The Ghosts are terrified of him and realize that the best course of action is to keep a low profile and avoid plotting against him, knowing that sooner or later he would find out anyway. WKX’s behavior is a source of deep disappointment for LFM; she remains silent, knowing her place, yet she understands that the boy she once tried to save has transformed into a ruthless man. I think she pities WKX for how he has ended up—for the way his time in that dreadful place has altered his character.

Gov. Alia Commends Professionalism of Pilot and NAF Support in Benue

​Governor Hyacinth Alia has commended the Nigerian Air Force pilot for the professionalism he demonstrated by exercising professional discretion to execute a precautionary landing approximately 10 nautical miles from the airfield in Makurdi.

​The Governor stated that the Nigerian Air Force (NAF) successfully provided close air support to surface forces during an operation targeting suspected kidnappers in the Ogbadigbo area of Benue State, near the Enugu–Benue boundary. He disclosed that the operation has disrupted the activities of criminal elements and supported the advance of surface forces.

​"It was on their way back to base that, in accordance with established operational and safety procedures, the pilot exercised his professional discretion to execute a precautionary landing," Governor Alia disclosed.

​This was contained in a statement released by Tersoo Kula, mnipr, Chief Press Secretary to the Governor of Benue State.

​The statement reads:

​The Governor further appreciates the NAF for its continued efforts to combat insecurity in Benue State.
​He describes the operation as a demonstration of the military’s determination to confront criminal elements and restore peace to troubled communities.

​He notes that the development offers renewed hope to residents affected by insecurity and reassures the people of Benue of his administration’s commitment to working with security agencies to address the challenges confronting the state.

​He praises the courage, commitment, and professionalism of NAF personnel in supporting ground troops and confronting threats to public safety.
​Governor Alia acknowledges the risks undertaken by officers and men of the service, describing their sacrifices as vital to the collective effort to secure Benue State and the country at large.

​He assures the Nigerian Air Force of Benue State’s continued support—alongside that of other security agencies—in the fight against criminality, emphasizing that sustained inter-agency collaboration is essential to protecting lives and property, containing criminal activities, and creating conditions for displaced communities to return home without fear.

​The Governor urges all security formations to remain relentless until criminal groups can no longer terrorize communities or disrupt the livelihoods of innocent citizens.

​He equally calls on residents to support ongoing security operations by providing credible and timely information to security operatives, stressing that the fight against insecurity requires collective responsibility.

​He reiterates his administration’s resolve to work with the military and other relevant authorities to achieve lasting peace and security across Benue State.

Lean Hog Futures Weekly Outlook: October 5 to 9, 2026

Top News Story: October Hogs Extend Losses Into Weekend as Cash Index Drops Under $79 Ahead of Expiration
The lean hog complex faced steady defensive pressure throughout the first full week of October, with active contracts posting weekly losses as cash fundamentals continued their seasonal decline. Benchmark October lean hogs extended lower into Friday's CME close, settling at 76.500 as traders actively enforced cash index convergence ahead of next week's expiration.

The primary driver behind the weak market tone was accelerating cash erosion paired with expanding fall slaughter supplies. The CME Lean Hog Index broke below the $79.00 threshold, sliding to $78.41 per cwt, while wholesale pork carcass cutout values tested multi month lows near $80.50. Increased packer processing runs provided ample meat volume to wholesale pipelines, limiting immediate buyer urgency for spot pork cuts.

With heavy autumn swine marketings moving through processing lines at full speed, speculative capital remained content to trim net long exposure and allow paper valuations to align with physical cash bids.

Market Notes
The CME Lean Hog Index maintained its seasonal trajectory downward, shedding another 50 cents to settle at $78.41 as of October 7. Negotiated cash procurement reflected this broader physical softness, though Friday morning's USDA national base hog price showed a late bounce to $74.46 per cwt, up $1.92 from Thursday.

Wholesale carcass values experienced continued pressure before stabilizing into the weekend. The USDA Friday morning pork carcass cutout value stood at $80.50 per cwt, supported by modest morning bounces across primal cuts after testing lower levels mid week.

Federally inspected slaughter runs remained heavy, with Wednesday processing estimated at 495,000 head, bringing week to date totals to 1.482 million head, up 26,000 head from the previous week and roughly 27,600 head above year ago levels.

Price Summary and Recent Movements
Futures prices extended losses into Friday's session, establishing lower weekly close settlements across nearby and deferred months. Performance metrics at the CME close on Friday, October 9, 2026:

October 2026 (HEV26): 76.500, down -0.550 (Daily), continuing its slide ahead of contract expiration.
December 2026 (HEZ26): 67.675, down -0.925 (Daily), pushing deeper into new multi month lows.

February 2027 (HEG27): 69.125, down -0.525 (Daily), consolidating within winter seasonal frames.
April 2027 (HEJ27): 74.200, down -0.650 (Daily), tracking long term trendlines.

Cash Trade: Friday morning national base price at $74.46; Friday morning pork carcass cutout value at $80.50.

Key Market Factors

Supply: Daily slaughter paces exceeding 495,000 head demonstrate heavy seasonal marketings, expanding wholesale pork availability and keeping physical cash bids defensive.

Demand: Export performance remains steady, with USDA Weekly Export Sales reporting 26,872 MT of pork sold for 2026 shipment, while actual shipments reached 32,803 MT led by buyers in Mexico.

External: Broader weakness across livestock and economic growth concerns kept speculative buying measured, though elevated retail beef prices continue to offer long term substitution support for pork.

Technicals: October hogs breached chart support near $77.00, while December hogs broke key support at $68.50, accelerating technical sell stops down to 67.675.

Upcoming USDA Reports Expectations
With October futures entering their final trading days before expiration, market focus is shifting completely toward the active December contract and weekly export movement. Traders will closely monitor whether post holiday retail pipeline replenishment prompts packers to defend cash bids or if swelling slaughter weights maintain pressure on wholesale cutout values.

Funds Activity
Managed money traders maintained a net selling orientation through the week as technical sell signals triggered across front month contracts. The failure of December hogs to hold support at $69.00 has kept institutional accounts strictly cautious, with funds awaiting a clear stabilization in the cash index before re entering on the long side.

Outlook for the Week Ahead
The near term trajectory remains neutral to soft as nearby contracts complete final cash convergence. A sustained daily close back above $69.00 in December hogs is required to signal short term stabilization, while further breakdown in wholesale cutout values could test lower seasonal chart bounds.

Risks: A breakdown below $67.00 in December hogs or continued slide in wholesale cutout values below $80.00.

Strategy: Defensive to cautious. Maintain strict risk management on long positions until technical indicators confirm a clear daily reversal above intermediate moving averages.

text:
I have said this thing countless times, but I’ll say it again for the umpteenth time: if you are still a student in Nigeria, learn a skill. It doesn’t matter whether you are studying Medicine or Microbiology. Learn a skill like your life depends on it. Lmao! Your life actually depends on it.

Life outside school is not a case of “done and dusted.” After you sign out and defend your project, you will regret not learning a skill or starting a small business while you were still in school.

I know this may sound annoying because, in a sane country, your degree should be enough to earn you an honest and decent living. But that is not the reality here. In fact, there is a high chance that you may not even use your certificate after graduation.

Medical doctors in Nigeria are juggling two or three jobs in different hospitals just to make ends meet. Many graduates have become WhatsApp vendors just to stay afloat.

Nigeria has no plan for you. Use that six-month IT period to multitask. Pick a skill, commit to it, and master it. If you are reading this as a student, you don’t know how privileged you are to have a stranger telling you this now.

The hand wey dey meet you for school now na less compared to wetin dey outside if you graduate without a skill. Learn one while it’s still early.

You see those months after graduation? Without a skill, you will find yourself depressed and/or confused. The parents and loved ones who used to send you allowances will stop because you are no longer a student. You’ll wake up every day feeling miserable as the reality that you are now on your own, and nobody is coming to save you, gradually dawns on you.

And that’s not even all. It gets worse after NYSC.

That is when you’ll fully realise that you are now an unemployed graduate. You can no longer say, “I’m a student” or “I’m waiting for service.” The pressure to move out of your parents’ house will start creeping in, especially when living there becomes uncomfortable and you realise you need to go out and make something of yourself.

But without a skill, where will you get the money to start building a life of your own?

Most jobs you’ll find in today’s market offer salaries of ₦100k–₦150k, with a “must have completed NYSC” requirement.

Now, let’s assume you are lucky enough to get a job that pays ₦150k monthly. Let’s do the maths:

Transportation: ₦3,000 daily × 5 days = ₦15,000 weekly. × 4 weeks = ₦60,000 monthly.

Feeding: ₦4,000 daily × 7 days = ₦28,000 weekly. × 4 weeks = ₦112,000 monthly.

Data: ₦5,000 weekly × 4 weeks = ₦20,000 monthly.

Total monthly expenses: ₦192,000.

Mind you, we haven’t even budgeted for rent, let alone electricity bills, groceries, clothes, other utilities, and black tax.

So, tell me, if you are lucky enough to land a job that pays ₦150k monthly, do you think you’ll escape the trenches with the calculations above?

The reality of life outside school is no joke. It is hard. Much harder than you can imagine while you’re still in school.

I’m not saying all these things to scare you. I’m telling you to prepare yourself to fight for your life after graduation.

Let me reiterate: irrespective of the course you are studying, learn a skill or start that small business while you’re still in school.

This is not a piece of advice. It is a warning.

I hope this tweet stays with you. Gracias.

text:
IN SHAKTA RECKONING, the Goddess is awake in spring and asleep in autumn. Worshipping her in Ashwin is akala, out of season. The explanation comes from Krittibas Ojha’s fifteenth-century Bengali Ramayan (the poet is dated to c. 1381–1461). Lanka will not fall. Brahma counsels Ram to wake the sleeping Goddess and undertake the rite. Ram vows to offer 108 blue lotuses. One is missing. Remembering that he is called Kamalanayana, the lotus-eyed, he raises an arrow to offer his own eye in place of the absent flower. The Goddess stops his hand and grants him victory. The 108 survive in Sandhi Puja, the charged junction between Ashtami and Navami.

This is Akalbodhon, the untimely awakening: we knock because Raghav knocked. Akala is more than a scheduling error. It is a crisis that forces someone to knock on a closed door. The permanent Mother was already there, in the seats where Sati’s body fell: Kamakhya, Kalighat, Tara Tarini, Vimala. The autumn Durga is the visiting daughter. Bengal welcomes her as Uma, the married daughter who comes without Shiva, with Ganesh, Kartik, Lakshmi and Saraswati beneath one frame, in its agamani songs. She is woken at a shut door and comes home anyway. Bengal’s festival has been shaped ever since by people standing outside doors, and by people trying to keep them shut.

ARTICLE 

NOBODY CARES ABOUT A MAN'S STRUGGLES UNTIL HE MAKES IT 💫💫

There is a side of being a man that people rarely talk about.

The side where you wake up every morning with responsibilities on your shoulders, bills waiting to be paid, dreams you are trying to achieve, and problems you cannot even explain to anybody.

You still have to show up.

You still have to smile.

You still have to act like everything is under control, even when you are trying to figure out your next move.

And the hardest part?

The world often celebrates the results without caring about the sacrifices it took to achieve them.

When a man is broke, people question his decisions.

When he is struggling, some call him lazy.

When he has nothing to offer financially, some people suddenly forget the good things about him.

But let that same man become successful, buy a house, drive a good car, and start making money. Suddenly, everybody wants to know his story.

They call him an inspiration.

They celebrate his journey.

They want to be associated with his success.

But where were they when he was struggling?

Where were they when he needed encouragement instead of judgment?

Where were they when he had big dreams but nothing in his pocket to prove them?

This is why every man needs to learn how to keep moving, even when nobody claps for him.

Not because he doesn't need love.

Not because he doesn't need support.

But because he cannot afford to make other people's approval the foundation of his life.

Build quietly.

Learn constantly.

Make mistakes, correct them, and keep going.

Don't let your current situation convince you that your story is over.

Being broke today doesn't mean you will be broke forever. Being rejected today doesn't mean you are unworthy. And struggling today doesn't mean you are a failure.

But remember something important: success is not just about proving people wrong. It is also about becoming the person you once prayed you could be.

Protect your peace. Take care of your mental health. Choose your circle wisely. And never be ashamed of honest work.

Your journey may be slow, but slow progress is still progress.

One day, let your life tell the story that your mouth was too tired to explain.

If you're a man fighting silent battles right now, keep going. Your struggles do not define your final destination.

And to everyone reading this: never look down on someone simply because they haven't made it yet. You don't know what they are fighting to overcome.

QUESTION: Do people genuinely support a man while he is struggling, or do most people only respect him after he becomes successful?

Let's talk in the comments. 👇

text:
THIS WEEK IN EL SALVADOR

Vol. 16 | October 4–10, 2026

Presidential approval, landmark gang convictions, economic growth, foreign investment, tourism, infrastructure and artificial intelligence.

El Salvador entered October with a series of developments spanning public opinion, justice, international investment, tourism, infrastructure and technology.

President Nayib Bukele topped a new international approval ranking. Two convicted MS-13 gang members received life sentences. The World Bank raised its economic growth forecast, Chevron announced plans for another major investment, and the country's principal international airport surpassed four million passengers.

Meanwhile, construction continued on a 50,000-seat national stadium, Honduran visitors arrived for Semana Morazánica, and Salvadoran institutions presented new tools to support investment and urban planning.

Together, these developments offer a broad picture of the issues shaping El Salvador's final quarter of 2026.

1. 🇸🇻 BUKELE LEADS INTERNATIONAL APPROVAL RANKING WITH 90%

President Nayib Bukele opened the week at the top of Mitofsky's latest international ranking of presidential approval.

According to the September 2026 results published by Mitofsky and TResearch, Bukele registered 90% approval, placing first among 40 national leaders evaluated worldwide.

The Salvadoran president responded to the results on X with a short message: “La cima es solitaria…” — “It's lonely at the top.”

The ranking represents another notable international public-opinion result for a president whose administration has placed security, infrastructure, investment and economic development at the center of its agenda.

2. ⚖️ HISTORIC LIFE SENTENCES FOR TWO MS-13 GANG MEMBERS
El Salvador's justice system delivered one of the week's most significant security developments on October 9.

The Fourth Organized Crime Court of San Salvador sentenced two members of MS-13 to life imprisonment.

The convicted men were identified as Josué Germain González Mejía, described by prosecutors as a corredor de clica, or clique-level leader, and Giovanni Andrés Hernández, identified as a homeboy, a recognized gang member.

According to the Attorney General's Office (FGR), prosecutors established that the defendants exercised criminal control over areas of San Salvador and surrounding communities. The prosecution linked their activities to homicides, disappearances, extortion and other organized-crime offenses.

Both men had been arrested under the state of exception introduced in March 2022 and subsequently prosecuted.

These are among the first life sentences imposed on MS-13 members under El Salvador's new sentencing framework, representing a notable development in the prosecution of organized crime. They were not, however, the country's first life sentences overall.

The development comes alongside other convictions. On October 8, the FGR reported that 52 members of the Soya Criminal Locos Salvatruchos clique, including six leaders, received sentences ranging from 20 to 48 years for crimes including illicit association, drug offenses, injuries and aggravated robbery.

Prosecutors said the group had operated in several Soyapango communities, including El Limón, Villa Kiwanis, Los Arenales, Santa Rosa and Guayacán.

These rulings illustrate how the country's security strategy continues to extend from arrests and territorial enforcement into the courtroom, with prosecutors seeking long-term sentences against convicted gang members.

3. 📈 WORLD BANK RAISES EL SALVADOR’S 2026 GROWTH FORECAST TO 4.5%

El Salvador received another important economic development this week as the World Bank raised its growth outlook for 2026 to 4.5%.

The updated forecast places El Salvador among the stronger-performing economies in Latin America this year and, according to the reporting released October 6, ahead of its Central American neighbors in projected economic expansion.

The World Bank identifies improving security conditions, stronger private investment, construction activity and consumption as important factors supporting the economy.

The institution also recognizes the importance of fiscal consolidation and continued reforms in strengthening economic stability and investor confidence.

The new projection follows an extended period of improving economic activity, including the expansion of construction, tourism and private investment.

President Bukele highlighted the revised forecast on X, drawing attention to the country's improved economic outlook.

For perspective, the World Bank reports that El Salvador's economy expanded by 3.9% in 2025, following 2.6% growth in 2024.

4. 💰 CHEVRON ANNOUNCES NEARLY $90 MILLION IN NEW INVESTMENT
International energy company Chevron announced plans to invest approximately $90 million in El Salvador.

According to the October 9 announcement, the investment will focus on expanding fuel-storage capacity and opening additional service stations in areas experiencing commercial and urban development.

The new commitment follows approximately $55 million invested by the company since 2020.

The expansion is relevant not only to the energy sector but also to transportation, logistics, commerce and the broader infrastructure supporting economic activity.

As new residential, industrial and commercial developments emerge, the country's fuel-distribution network must also adapt to changing demand.

Chevron's announcement adds another major corporate investment plan to El Salvador's growing pipeline of private-sector projects.

5. 🇺🇸 US INVESTMENT IN EL SALVADOR RISES 60.5%

United States investment provided another encouraging economic headline.

According to figures reported by Diario El Mundo on October 4, US investment in El Salvador increased by 60.5%, reaching its highest reported investment position since late 2018.

Between April and June 2026, capital flows from the United States totaled approximately $144.41 million.

The development is especially relevant because the United States remains one of El Salvador's most important commercial and financial partners.

In a separate report published October 5, US authorities highlighted elements of El Salvador's investment framework, including dollarization, legal protections for investors and legislation supporting investment banking and alternative investment funds.

Together, these developments point to increasing interest in El Salvador's financial and business environment.

The reported capital flows and investment position are distinct measures, but both contribute to the broader picture of US economic engagement with El Salvador.

6. 🏗️ CHINA-DONATED NATIONAL STADIUM REACHES 75% COMPLETION

One of the country's most visible infrastructure projects continues moving toward completion.

The new national stadium, donated by the People's Republic of China, has reached approximately 75% construction progress.

Chinese Ambassador Zhang Yanhui reported that the stadium's seating was scheduled to arrive during the October 10–11 weekend, marking another stage in the development of the facility.

Designed to accommodate approximately 50,000 spectators, the stadium is intended to become a major venue for football, international sporting competitions and large-scale public events.

Beyond its seating capacity, the project represents a significant addition to El Salvador's sports and entertainment infrastructure.

When completed, the stadium could strengthen the country's ability to host events attracting regional and international visitors, supporting tourism, hospitality and related services.

The project also stands among the most recognizable examples of infrastructure cooperation between El Salvador and China.

7. ✈️ EL SALVADOR INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT SURPASSES FOUR MILLION PASSENGERS

El Salvador's principal international airport passed another important milestone this week.

By October 8, the airport had handled more than four million passengers in 2026, according to figures reported by Diario El Mundo.

The total includes passenger traffic associated with international travel, connections and transfers, reflecting the airport's role as both a Salvadoran gateway and a regional aviation hub.

Growing air connectivity is particularly important for tourism, international business, Salvadorans living abroad and commercial activity.

The milestone also reinforces the importance of continued airport modernization as passenger demand expands.

For El Salvador, an increasingly connected airport system is part of a wider effort to strengthen the country's position within Central American transportation and tourism networks.

8. 🛫 PACIFIC AIRPORT TERMINAL REACHES 30.14% CONSTRUCTION PROGRESS

Progress was also reported at the future Pacific Airport.

The construction of the airport's Beta terminal building reached 30.14%.

Work on the terminal's steel structure is expected to conclude in December 2026, while the first stage of the airport project is scheduled for mid-2027.

The Pacific Airport is intended to improve air connectivity in eastern El Salvador, a region with significant potential for tourism, commerce and investment.

Its development is particularly relevant to areas connected to the country's eastern coastline and the wider Surf City tourism strategy.

Although the project remains under construction, the reported progress offers a measurable update on one of El Salvador's major transportation investments.

9. 🇭🇳 MORE THAN 43,400 HONDURANS VISIT EL SALVADOR DURING SEMANA MORAZÁNICA

Thousands of Honduran visitors crossed into El Salvador during Semana Morazánica, the annual holiday period in Honduras.

By midday on October 8, Salvadoran migration authorities had recorded more than 43,400 entries by Honduran citizens, already exceeding the 43,008 recorded during the comparable 2025 holiday period.

The largest daily influx occurred on October 7, when more than 8,600 Honduran visitors entered the country.

Visitors traveled to enjoy beaches, restaurants, mountains, historic districts and other destinations.

Some were also drawn to the newly inaugurated Francisco Morazán mausoleum in San Salvador's historic center, connecting this week's tourism activity with last week's commemoration of the Central American leader.

The Salvadoran migration authority reported an expected total of approximately 48,300 entries for the holiday period, although one newspaper account cited a higher projection. The final result should be assessed against the official closing figure.

The influx is another example of the growing importance of regional tourism to El Salvador's hospitality and service industries.

10. 🏨 JW MARRIOTT SAN SALVADOR TAKES SHAPE AT MULTIPLAZA

El Salvador's luxury hospitality sector is preparing for another major addition.

The JW Marriott San Salvador project, located at Multiplaza, presented model rooms this week, offering an early look at the development's planned accommodations.

The project is designed to include 186 guest rooms and a theater, combining upscale hospitality with facilities that could support business travel, entertainment and events.

The investment reflects interest in higher-end accommodations as El Salvador attracts international travelers, business delegations and visitors seeking premium experiences.

The development also contributes to the broader transformation of the San Salvador metropolitan area's commercial and hospitality infrastructure.

For a country expanding its international tourism profile, new hotel capacity is an important component of long-term destination development.

11. 🏭 SALVADORAN INDUSTRY GROWS 3.6%

El Salvador's industrial sector recorded growth of 3.6%, according to figures highlighted by Diario El Salvador on October 6.

The sector accounts for approximately 12.7% of national gross domestic product, underscoring its importance to employment, production and the wider economy.

Industrial activity contributes to domestic supply chains while also supporting exports and the development of new commercial opportunities.

Its performance matters because a growing economy requires more than tourism and construction alone.

Manufacturing, industrial production, logistics and related services provide another foundation for economic diversification and formal employment.

The latest figures suggest that industry remains an important contributor to El Salvador's economic activity during 2026.

12. ₿ A NEW CHIVO SEEKS TO EXPAND FINANCIAL INCLUSION

El Salvador's Bitcoin and digital-finance sector also made headlines this week.

The new Chivo initiative presented plans to offer free remittances from the United States and expand access to credit for Salvadorans, including individuals without traditional banking relationships.

The proposal is significant because remittances remain an important source of household income for Salvadoran families.

Reducing transfer costs could allow recipients to retain more of the funds sent by relatives abroad.

Access to credit is another major element of the initiative, particularly for people who have historically faced barriers to conventional financial services.

The announcement outlines the new platform's ambitions; the practical impact will depend on its rollout, eligibility requirements and actual adoption.

Nevertheless, the project reflects continued efforts to connect digital financial services with everyday economic needs.

13. 🤖 LUIS RODRÍGUEZ PRESENTS NIX: AI FOR INVESTMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL PLANNING

Artificial intelligence is increasingly becoming part of El Salvador's institutional planning.

Luis Rodríguez, Executive Director of the San Salvador Metropolitan Area Planning Office (OPAMSS), presented NIX, an artificial-intelligence platform designed to support investment planning and environmental sustainability.

The presentation took place during the First Congress on Decentralized Cooperation in El Salvador.

According to @LRodriguez_SV, NIX is intended to improve strategic decision-making by providing territorial information relevant to investment and development across the San Salvador Metropolitan Area and the coastal region of La Libertad.

The initiative was developed with support from the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID), with Rodríguez also recognizing cooperation involving ESCO and the Embassy of Spain in El Salvador.

The significance of NIX extends beyond the introduction of another technology platform.

Urban development requires decisions involving land use, infrastructure, environmental conditions, economic opportunities and the long-term needs of growing communities.

AI-assisted planning tools could help public institutions and investors evaluate these factors more effectively.

For @COAMSS_OPAMSS, the initiative represents a new application of technology to territorial management and investment facilitation.

14. 🏘️ HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT REMAIN ON THE INTERNATIONAL AGENDA

El Salvador's housing and construction institutions continued participating in international cooperation and investment discussions.

Housing Minister @misol140, OPAMSS Executive Director Luis Rodríguez, representatives of the Salvadoran Chamber of Construction (@CASALCOsv) and business leaders participated in the Inter-American Development Bank's Housing Forum 2026.

The agenda included meetings and exchanges focused on housing development and opportunities for cooperation.

In another institutional activity, Tourism Minister @MorenaValdezSV joined Rodríguez, Adriana Larín of the Historic Center Authority (@AutoridadchSV), Paola Bardi of the DOT, business representatives and construction-sector technicians for a practical workshop.

These engagements highlight the relationship between housing, urban development, tourism and the investment climate.

As construction activity expands, coordination among public institutions, developers and international partners becomes increasingly relevant to the planning and execution of new projects.

THE BIGGER PICTURE: A COUNTRY BUILDING ACROSS MULTIPLE SECTORS

This week's headlines are notable not because they all concern one subject, but because they reflect developments across many parts of Salvadoran life.

A president leading an international approval ranking.

Two MS-13 members receiving life sentences.

A World Bank growth forecast raised to 4.5%.

Chevron announcing nearly $90 million in investment.

US investment figures showing renewed momentum.

A 50,000-seat stadium reaching 75% completion.

An international airport surpassing four million passengers.

Thousands of Hondurans crossing the border to spend their holidays in El Salvador.

New luxury accommodations, industrial growth, digital financial services and artificial-intelligence tools for urban planning.

Each story represents a different part of the country's economic, institutional and social landscape.

Taken together, they show a nation pursuing major projects while confronting the continuing challenges of economic development, public security and institutional modernization.

El Salvador's transformation is no longer a story confined to one headline. It is unfolding across airports, construction sites, courtrooms, businesses, tourist destinations and technology platforms.

And this week provided another opportunity to see that broader picture.

text:
📌 Wall Street's products, rebuilt as tokens.

Save this — Ondo Finance (@Ondo) explained from the primary sources: the products holding nearly $4B, the US license stack it owns outright, and what the token actually governs.

1. What Ondo Is
Ondo Finance is a tokenization company. It takes products Wall Street already sells (Treasury funds, a yield-bearing dollar, household-name stocks) and reissues them as tokens on public blockchains, where they can be held, moved and redeemed well beyond market hours.

2. The Products (Ondo's own site, checked Oct 9, 2026)
• OUSG — a tokenized fund of short-term US Treasuries ($319M), for qualified investors. Its portfolio is invested in funds issued by BlackRock (@BlackRock) (including BlackRock's BUIDL fund), Franklin Templeton (@FranklnTempletn), WisdomTree (@WisdomTreeFunds), Fidelity (@Fidelity) and others, alongside bank deposits and USDC held for liquidity.
• USDY — Ondo's own word is "yieldcoin" ($2.32B): a tokenized note backed by US Treasuries and bank deposits. Ondo is explicit that it is not a stablecoin. Offered to non-US investors.
• Ondo Stocks — 450+ tokenized US stocks and ETFs ($1.33B, ~245,100 holders). The tokens (TSLAon, SPYon and the like) are designed to give the same economic exposure as owning the stock, dividends reinvested: not direct title, and no shareholder voting rights. Launched Sep 3, 2025 with 100+ tickers; crossed $1B in under eight months. Not available in the US.

3. How It Works
Money comes in through regulated entities; the real asset (fund shares, Treasuries, listed stock held via US-registered broker-dealers) sits in custody; the token is issued as the onchain claim and can be minted or redeemed 24/7 on supported products. For Ondo's tokenized stocks and ETFs, prices and corporate actions like dividends and splits are fed by Chainlink (@chainlink), named Ondo's official oracle and data standard for those products in an Oct 2025 strategic partnership, the plumbing that decides whether a tokenized dividend lands correctly.

4. The License Stack (the actual moat)
Most tokenization startups rent compliance. Ondo bought it. In Oct 2025 it completed the acquisition of Oasis Pro: a broker-dealer, an alternative trading system (ATS) and a transfer agent, each registered with the SEC (@SECGov), owned outright. In July 2026 its broker-dealer subsidiary, Oasis Pro Markets, received FINRA (@FINRA) authorizations to offer tokenized equities and funds to US financial institutions and retail investors. And in April 2025, Ondo's team sat with the SEC's Crypto Task Force to present its proposal for issuing and selling wrapped, tokenized versions of publicly traded US securities — the meeting memo is public at the SEC.

5. Who's Plugging In
• DTCC (@The_DTCC) — in Sep 2026, Oasis Pro Markets joined DTCC's Fund/SERV as a member: the first tokenization platform on the network that processes more than 85% of US mutual fund transaction activity. Separately, Ondo Stocks representations have been issued through DTC tokenized entitlements (Jul 2026).
• Mastercard (@Mastercard) — Ondo joined Mastercard's Multi-Token Network in Feb 2025 as its first real-world-asset provider, with OUSG the first tokenized RWA on the network.
• J.P. Morgan (@jpmorgan) Kinexys — in May 2025, Kinexys, Chainlink and Ondo completed a cross-chain delivery-versus-payment test transaction using OUSG, on Ondo Chain testnet. A test transaction, not production volume.

6. The Token
$ONDO is the governance token of the Ondo DAO and of Flux Finance, the lending protocol where tokenized securities can serve as collateral (the Ondo Foundation's own docs' wording). Initial supply: 10 billion, increasable only by a majority vote of holders, per the Foundation's own risk factors. Holders vote on protocol parameters and upgrades.

The Fine Print
The names above are fund issuers, network operators and test counterparties, each relationship stated exactly as its source states it. BlackRock's role is the narrowest of them: it issues a fund in OUSG's portfolio. That is a holding, not an endorsement, and BlackRock has said nothing about $ONDO. Stock tokens are economic exposure held through custody, not shares in your name. $ONDO governs a DAO; it carries no claim on product revenue or yield (the Foundation's own risk factors say so). Figures are Ondo's published snapshots from Oct 9, 2026 (they move).

In Plain English
• Ondo reissues Wall Street's existing products as blockchain tokens: same assets, new rails — beyond market hours, programmable, reachable on public chains.
• Its edge is not the tokens. It is owning the US licenses and sitting inside the networks (DTCC, Mastercard) the old system already runs on.

Why This Is Bullish
Institutions keep writing Ondo into official infrastructure: a DTCC network membership, a Mastercard network slot, an SEC meeting on the public record. Receipts like that are how a niche product becomes plumbing.

My Take:
Everyone argues about which assets get tokenized. Ondo quietly bought the cash register, the shop license and a seat in the mall. Whoever wins the argument still has to settle somewhere — Ondo is building the somewhere.

If your stocks and Treasury funds could move at 2 AM on a Sunday, what would you actually do differently — and which product do you think should stay in the old system forever?
