text:
(Full article here, just in case...)
1. Evidence over eminence
Clinical expertise is indispensable. Real patients do not resemble textbook cases, and judgment is needed to translate evidence into care. The risk is that practice-informed wisdom can become difficult to distinguish from inherited practice when the underlying evidence is neither visible nor continuously updated.
Evidence over eminence. Evidence in the hands of experts.
Health decisions draw on knowledge across specialties, guidelines, trials, diagnostic methods, and emerging research. No individual can continuously absorb every relevant publication across every domain that may affect one person's long-term health.
The central proposition is:
The science available to an individual should extend beyond the field of view of any one expert.
Choosing the best expert and finding the best available science are different problems. AI begins to separate them by expanding the field of view available to individuals and experts while preserving the judgment, accountability, and human context that health decisions require.
2. The bandwidth problem
The internet solved access to health information. It did not solve the decision problem.
Consider two people with the same serious diagnosis. One happens to see a physician connected to an academic center running a clinical trial for which they may be eligible. The other sees an equally capable physician whose network does not include that trial. The trial may ultimately be appropriate, inappropriate, beneficial, or ineffective, but only one person is likely to know that option exists. Their biology may be similar. Their field of possible action is not. Bandwidth creates the difference.
A person can now find thousands of papers, guidelines, product claims, podcasts, and AI-generated explanations. Search can identify something that might matter, but it rarely establishes:
what the evidence actually demonstrated and how credible it is;
whether the studied population resembles this person and the finding supports an intervention;
whether the likely benefit justifies the risk, burden, cost, or opportunity cost; or
what deserves attention before other plausible actions.
The harder problem is determining which few possibilities deserve attention now, which require more information, and which should not enter the plan. Science exceeds the attention available to evaluate it, while possible actions exceed the time and capacity available to perform them.
The question is no longer only, “What does my expert know?” It becomes, “What does science know that matters to me?”
3. AI changes what is possible
AI can monitor literature, discover relevant sources, extract structured claims, compare findings, identify conflicts, preserve provenance, and generate explanations from an inspectable decision record. This allows a system to continually ask which evidence may be relevant to a defined person and decision.
The distinction is fundamental:
Search finds information about a question.
General-purpose AI synthesizes an answer to a question.
A health-maximization system continuously identifies and ranks which questions and actions may matter for a person—even when they did not know to ask—and makes them available for expert judgment and subject choice.
The system must also determine whether something else matters more.
A reliable system treats the model as an interpreter rather than the source of truth. Its output depends on the evidence retrieved, the distinctions preserved, the subject data interpreted, and the rules governing downstream use. A general-purpose model may summarize an observational association as advice, apply a trial outside its studied population, or treat one statistically significant result as settled science.
Health maximization therefore requires more than conversational intelligence. It requires a governed path from source evidence to personal action, with uncertainty and provenance carried through every step.
As these systems become demonstrably reliable, the question may increasingly shift from whether AI should support expert assessment to where such support improves completeness, consistency, and decision quality.
4. What health maximization means
Health maximization applies decision science to choices made under uncertainty.

The person supplies the ends. Health matters in part because it supports the relationships, activities, ambitions, independence, and experiences that matter to the individual. The system therefore allocates limited health effort in service of the life that person values, rather than maximizing biomarkers, interventions, or health activity in the abstract.

This changes how value is assessed. A marginal improvement in a health metric may not justify the time, attention, or capacity it consumes. Conversely, preserving a capability central to a person's goals may be highly valuable even when no universal health score captures that value.
At any point in time, a person faces a distribution of possible future outcomes. An action may shift that distribution, leave it largely unchanged, or introduce new benefits and harms. The relevant question is not whether an action is generically healthy. It is whether the available evidence suggests that including it in this person's portfolio is more valuable than the alternatives.
You cannot choose the outcome. You can choose how to shift the odds.
An exercise intervention may improve expected fitness while introducing injury risk and consuming time that could have been spent elsewhere. A therapy may reduce one risk while increasing another. A diagnostic may provide no direct health benefit yet still be valuable if its result changes a consequential decision.
Health maximization manages a portfolio of probabilities across the outcomes an individual values. It selects actions that shift plausible outcomes in a preferred direction while accounting for uncertainty, risk, cost, burden, and trade-offs.

A scientifically faithful recommendation explains which outcomes may change, the expected magnitude and uncertainty of the shift, and the risks or opportunities that accompany the choice.
This framing has several consequences.
First, the output is a portfolio rather than a single recommendation. Exercise, medication discussions, sleep, diagnostics, nutrition, mental health, and monitoring may compete for the same limited time and attention.
Second, doing nothing is a legitimate option. An intervention can be biologically plausible yet too uncertain, burdensome, risky, or low-value to prioritize.
Third, measurement can itself be an action. When a missing observation could materially change the choice, obtaining that information may be more valuable than immediately choosing an intervention.
Finally, the answer is expected to change. New evidence, measurements, goals, constraints, and observed outcomes can alter both the probabilities and the preferred portfolio.
5. The architecture
The architecture separates two questions that are often collapsed: What does science support? and What does it imply for this person now?
        SCIENCE UNIVERSE                      SUBJECT UNIVERSE
    What could work, for whom?             What is true of this person?

    Discover relevant evidence             Measure observations
              ↓                                      ↓
    Evaluate and synthesize                Consolidate longitudinal context
              ↓                                      ↓
    Preserve uncertainty and provenance    Structure state, goals,
              ↓                            capabilities, risks, and missingness
              └──────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                                 ↓
                         DECISION LAYER
                    Match · Prioritize · Explain
                                 ↓
                         ACTION PORTFOLIO
                  Do · Measure · Ask · Avoid · Defer
                                 ↓
                   Expert judgment + subject choice
                                 ↓
                   New evidence + observed outcomes
                                 ↺
                        Update and re-evaluate
The two universes remain separate because scientific credibility and personal relevance are different judgments. Strong evidence may apply poorly to a person. A highly relevant hypothesis may still be too uncertain to justify action.
Context is a decision input rather than a third knowledge universe. Current time, money, access, burden, capacity, and decision-specific preferences change what is feasible and valuable now; they do not change what a study found. This separation allows a priority to change without silently rewriting the science.
Elyx is building this architecture into the operating system behind its members' healthspan programs, connecting evaluated evidence with a continually updated representation of each member to support decisions about what to investigate, prioritize, execute, measure, or defer.
6. The Science Universe
The Science Universe turns a changing evidence corpus into evaluated knowledge through four responsibilities.
Discover broadly. Search across trials, reviews, guidelines, registries, and emerging research. Public commentary can surface an idea, but the underlying source must be inspected before it enters the trusted knowledge layer.
Evaluate rigorously. Determine what each source actually supports, for which population and outcome, with what effect estimate, uncertainty, limitations, and possible bias. Assessment belongs at the level of a specific claim—not merely the reputation of a paper or journal.[1,2]
Synthesize before personalizing. One exciting paper should not become one exciting recommendation. Findings must be interpreted alongside the broader evidence, and confidence in the evidence must remain distinct from the decision to act.
Preserve provenance. Every consequential conclusion remains traceable to its scientific basis and transformation history.
Different evidence supports different inferences:

Evidence says
The system may infer
A well-conducted randomized study found that an intervention changed an outcome in a studied population.
A candidate action, if applicability and safety support it.
An exposure is associated with an outcome.
A risk signal, not proof that changing the exposure changes the outcome.
A biological mechanism is plausible.
A hypothesis to investigate, not an intervention.
A clinical trial exists and a person may be eligible.
An opportunity to evaluate, not evidence that the treatment works.

AI must preserve the boundary between what was observed and what may responsibly be done.
7. The Subject Universe
The Subject Universe is a longitudinal, quality-aware representation organized around information that can affect a decision.
Potential inputs include medical history, symptoms, diagnoses, laboratory tests, imaging, medications, genetics, wearable and behavioral data, functional capacity, goals, valued capabilities, and longer-term preferences. Personal goals help define which health outcomes matter. The system preserves when and how an observation was produced, how reliable it is, and what remains missing or disputed.

Goals can be represented as a hierarchy rather than a flat list of health targets. What a person wants their life to enable can imply valued capabilities and intermediate health goals, which then affect the value of measurements and actions. A desire to continue travelling independently, for example, may imply goals related to mobility, strength, cardiovascular capacity, and disease risk. This preserves a traceable path from what matters to the person to what enters the action portfolio.
More data is not automatically better. The question is whether an observation is valid enough, current enough, and relevant enough to change a decision.
This creates a simple but consequential inversion: your data becomes a query into relevant scientific evidence. The Subject Universe asks which study populations, eligibility conditions, outcomes, and safety constraints resemble the present decision—and which mismatches should reduce confidence or trigger expert review.
8. Match, Prioritize, Explain
This is the core of the architecture. The Science Universe may produce many credible possibilities. The decision layer determines which matter for this person now.
Match
Does this science apply to me?
A study can be excellent science and still be poor evidence for this person. Match considers whether the studied population, baseline risk, intervention, outcome, dose, setting, and time horizon resemble the present decision. It also considers contraindications, interactions, evidence certainty, and missing information.
The same relative effect can produce very different absolute benefit in two people when their baseline risks differ. Estimating the likely shift therefore depends on both the effect supported by the evidence and the person's baseline risk.[3,4]
Where the evidence supports quantitative inference, Match estimates how an action may shift relevant outcomes, carrying the available uncertainty forward rather than producing a point promise. Where the evidence is sparse or indirect, it can produce a bounded qualitative assessment. Where a responsible inference is not possible, it can abstain or propose a measurement, question, or expert review.
Prioritize
Among everything that could help, what matters most now?
Prioritization is a constrained optimization problem. It compares these possible shifts across actions and outcomes in relation to the capabilities and health outcomes the person values. Every person has finite time, money, attention, access, and tolerance for risk, so candidate actions must be compared across expected benefit and harm, evidence certainty, urgency, reversibility, information value, burden, feasibility, interactions, and personal preference.[2,5,6]
Those dimensions should not disappear inside one unexplained health score. Outcomes such as mobility, sleep, cardiovascular risk, diagnostic information, time, and burden are not naturally interchangeable.
The portfolio makes the cut line visible: what deserves attention now, what becomes worthwhile if capacity expands, and what should currently be deferred. The line can move. More time or budget may raise an action; a contraindication may lower it; a measurement may resolve enough uncertainty to promote an action—or show that it should be dropped.
Explain
Why—and what could change the answer?
Explain derives from the decision record behind the ranking. It identifies the intended outcome, evidence that influenced the result, subject factors affecting applicability, expected benefits and harms, uncertainty, constraints, alternatives, and information that could change the decision.
An explanation should make disagreement possible. A reviewer should be able to challenge the evidence, change an assumption or preference, and see whether the portfolio changes for the right reason.
9. An illustrative case: competing priorities
Consider a 52-year-old who feels healthy, has a family history of cardiovascular disease and dementia, travels frequently, sleeps poorly, has elevated ApoB, and exercises three times a week. They can devote four hours a week to their health and are willing to spend substantially, but they do not want managing their health to consume the life that health is meant to enable.
The available questions multiply quickly. Should the fourth exercise hour go to aerobic conditioning or strength? Does creatine belong in the portfolio? Is an advanced cardiovascular test likely to change management? Does sleep deserve attention first? Which emerging diagnostics are decision-changing rather than merely interesting? What is not worth doing?
A search engine can return evidence for every item. A clinician may offer strong judgment within a domain. A general-purpose AI can produce a plausible list. None necessarily resolves the competition among actions.

Suppose the person's available bandwidth allows only three priorities to receive meaningful attention this month. The system's task is to identify which three priorities most deserve that capacity, which uncertainties should be resolved before further effort is committed, and which otherwise reasonable actions can wait.
The architecture might organize the possibilities this way:

Possible action
Illustrative placement
Reasoning pattern
Cardiovascular risk review
Review now
Existing risk signals could make qualified assessment decision-changing.
Sleep assessment
Investigate now
Better characterization could affect several outcomes and the feasibility of other actions.
Fourth exercise hour
Optimize now
Compare the marginal value and feasibility of aerobic and strength work for the person's goals.
Advanced diagnostic
Conditional
Valuable only if a plausible result would change management.
Creatine
Consider later
A relevant evidence signal exists, but its marginal value may be lower than unresolved higher-priority questions.
Novel intervention
Defer
Direct evidence, applicability, or safety may be insufficient.

The product of the system is not more health information. It is decision compression: from everything that might matter to the few things that matter now. In this illustration, three priorities receive attention now, one remains conditional, and two wait. The value is not the exact ordering implied by a handful of facts, but a reviewable account of what deserves attention, what should be measured, and what can wait.
Three months later, the portfolio may be different. New sleep data may change the assessment. Adherence may reveal that a plan is unrealistic. A laboratory value, new paper, symptom, or travel schedule may move the cut line. The system should explain why the portfolio changed rather than simply returning a new list.
This table illustrates the decision structure; it is not a clinical recommendation.
10. AI and expert judgment
AI can take on high-bandwidth scientific work: searching, extracting, comparing, monitoring, and maintaining structured evidence. Qualified experts contribute judgment wherever interpretation or decision-making is consequential: challenging assumptions, interpreting ambiguity and clinical context, managing safety, resolving disagreement, and caring for the person.
The first beneficiary of a health-maximization system is therefore the expert. Instead of asking one person to remember and reconcile every relevant field, the system provides an evidence-linked decision record that can be inspected, corrected, approved, rejected, or deferred.
Today, AI prepares; qualified experts decide. Over time, AI can handle more scientific interpretation while expert attention concentrates on ambiguity, consequence, judgment, and human care.
Oversight should be proportional to consequence. Routine processing can use automated checks and sampled human review. High-consequence interventions, safety concerns, conflicting evidence, population mismatch, novel therapies, and unresolved disagreement require review or escalation to an appropriately qualified professional.
11. A continuously learning system
The architecture operates as a loop because neither science nor people remain static.
Observe → update evidence or subject state → re-match → re-prioritize → decide → act → observe
A new study can change confidence in an intervention. A laboratory result can change estimated risk. Attempted adherence can change the expected feasibility of a plan. An injury, symptom, new goal, or change in budget can move the cut line.
The system should not defend its previous answer. It should show what changed, how that change affected the reasoning, and why the portfolio moved. An observed improvement should not automatically be attributed to the preceding action: concurrent changes, natural variation, measurement error, and regression to the mean can all mislead.
A system supporting consequential health decisions must itself be evaluated. Each stage—from evidence retrieval through matching, prioritization, and explanation—should be tested against expert review, and higher-consequence uses should face progressively stronger standards of prospective evaluation.[7–10] The same principle applied to the science should apply to the AI: confidence is not evidence of correctness.
Conclusion
AI expands the scale at which scientific evidence can be connected to an individual. Combined with a structured, continually updated understanding of that person, it becomes possible to ask repeatedly: what does the world's evolving scientific knowledge imply for this person now?
Turning retrieval into responsible action requires an architecture that evaluates before it personalizes, separates association from intervention, distinguishes credibility from applicability, allocates limited resources across competing actions, explains uncertainty, and identifies where human judgment is required.
Elyx is developing one implementation of this architecture. The broader idea is larger than any single product: every person could have a system continuously expanding the science available to them while helping their experts determine what deserves attention.
At sufficient scale, this relationship could eventually run in both directions. A system repeatedly asking what matters for individuals will also encounter the boundaries of existing knowledge—populations insufficiently studied, interventions never compared, and consequential questions science cannot yet answer. Aggregated responsibly, those gaps could help identify where new research would have the greatest value.
The question, “What does science know that matters to me?” therefore eventually reveals another: “What does science not yet know that matters to me?”
The promise of AI in health is a more complete, disciplined, and continually updated relationship between each person, their experts, and science.
That is the architecture of health maximization.

text:
The first reading for Saturday October 10, 2026: Book of Galatians (Galatians 3:22-29)

The law confined all under sin as prisoners awaiting freedom

Faith in Jesus Christ arrived to justify and adopt them as children of God

Baptized into Christ they became one with no divisions left as heirs to the promise

This is the message of Galatians 3:22-29

Embracing the Freedom That Comes Through Faith Alone

The letter to the Galatians stands as a powerful reminder that true liberty flows from trusting in Christ rather than relying on human efforts or traditions. In this reflection we explore how Paul guides believers toward a deeper understanding of grace that transforms daily living. His words invite faithful Catholics to examine their own approach to faith and community life. Through careful attention to each part of the message we can see how these ancient insights still shape our spiritual journey today.

What Does It Mean to Live Free From the Law

Paul opens by stressing that believers have been called to freedom yet must not use that freedom as an opportunity for self indulgence. He reminds the community that the whole law finds its fulfillment in loving one another as oneself. This teaching encourages Catholics to move beyond mere rule keeping and instead cultivate genuine charity in every interaction. The apostle warns against returning to the yoke of slavery that comes from trying to earn salvation through works alone. Such an approach risks diminishing the gift already received through the cross. By focusing on love as the guiding principle believers discover a freedom that strengthens rather than weakens their moral life.

How Can We Walk by the Spirit in Everyday Choices

The reading continues with a contrast between the desires of the flesh and the fruit produced by the Spirit. Paul lists attitudes that lead to division and contrasts them with qualities such as patience kindness and self control. For practicing Catholics this section offers practical guidance on discerning daily decisions at work and at home. Choosing to respond with gentleness instead of anger reflects the Spirit at work within the heart. Over time these small choices build a character that witnesses to the gospel in the wider world. The text reassures readers that those who belong to Christ have crucified the flesh with its passions and desires. This ongoing process requires vigilance yet brings lasting peace.

Why Does Community Life Depend on Mutual Support

Paul urges the Galatians to restore anyone caught in a transgression with a spirit of gentleness while watching their own conduct. He emphasizes bearing one another's burdens as a way of fulfilling the law of Christ. In Catholic parishes this call translates into practical acts of mercy such as visiting the sick or mentoring younger members of the faith. When individuals focus only on their own tasks they miss the opportunity to strengthen the body of Christ. The apostle also cautions against comparing oneself with others because each person must carry their own load. Such balance between personal responsibility and communal care creates an environment where faith can flourish across generations.

How Does Perseverance Lead to a Harvest of Righteousness

The final section encourages believers not to grow weary in doing what is right because in due time they will reap if they do not give up. Paul highlights the importance of doing good to all people especially those in the household of faith. Catholics can apply this by remaining steadfast in prayer and charitable works even when results seem slow to appear. The image of sowing to the Spirit points toward eternal life as the ultimate reward. This perspective helps maintain hope during seasons of trial or spiritual dryness. By keeping eternity in view the faithful find strength to continue their journey with renewed purpose.

The message from Galatians ultimately draws Catholics back to the core of their identity as children of God. Through faith they receive adoption and the Spirit who enables them to cry out Abba Father. This relationship frees them from fear and empowers them to live with confidence. As they reflect on these truths they are invited to renew their commitment to love service and perseverance. The letter closes with a blessing that underscores the grace available to all who walk according to this rule. In this way the reading continues to inspire generations of believers toward a life marked by authentic freedom and generous charity.
Finding Unity as God's Children in All Relationships

In the hustle of modern life faithful Catholics seek guidance from scripture to navigate interactions with loved ones and colleagues alike. The reading from Galatians provides a profound message about faith transcending divisions. By reflecting on these verses individuals discover fresh perspectives on unity and belonging. This exploration breaks down the text section by section while considering practical applications in various spheres of life. Through careful analysis readers can see how ancient words speak to contemporary challenges in building harmonious relationships.

What Insights Does Galatians Offer for Our Daily Walk

The passage opens by noting that scripture has imprisoned all things under the power of sin so that what was promised through faith in Jesus Christ might be given to those who believe. This sets a foundation of shared human limitation that calls for humility in every encounter. Before faith came people were imprisoned and guarded under the law until faith would be revealed. Such words remind readers that past structures no longer define worth allowing fresh approaches to conversations at home or work. Therefore the law was our disciplinarian until Christ came so that we might be justified by faith. This transition invites a shift from rigid expectations to grace filled exchanges that ease tensions among family members or neighbors.

But now that faith has come we are no longer subject to a disciplinarian for in Christ Jesus you are all children of God through faith. As many as were baptized into Christ have clothed themselves with Christ. These lines emphasize a new identity that overrides old categories fostering patience when disagreements arise with friends or co workers. There is no longer Jew or Greek there is no longer slave or free there is no longer male and female for all of you are one in Christ Jesus. This unity encourages seeing others beyond surface differences promoting inclusive dialogue in community settings. And if you belong to Christ then you are Abraham's offspring heirs according to the promise. Such inheritance language inspires a sense of shared legacy that motivates supportive actions toward those nearby.

How Can This Passage Deepen Family Connections

Within the home the emphasis on becoming children of God encourages parents to view children as fellow heirs rather than subordinates leading to more collaborative decision making during meals or chores. Siblings might draw on the removal of divisions to resolve conflicts with greater empathy avoiding favoritism that once strained bonds. The clothing with Christ image suggests wrapping daily routines in kindness such as offering help without expectation during busy evenings. This approach transforms ordinary interactions into opportunities for mutual growth and lasting affection.

In What Ways Does It Enhance Friendships and Neighborly Ties

Friends benefit from the promise of justification by faith which prompts listening without judgment when personal struggles surface during casual gatherings. Neighbors can apply the oneness in Christ to bridge cultural gaps perhaps through shared community projects that celebrate common humanity. The disciplinarian concept reminds individuals to release old grudges allowing forgiveness to flow naturally in block parties or casual chats over fences. Such practices build trust that extends beyond polite exchanges into genuine support networks.

How Might It Influence Workplace Relationships

At the office the absence of distinctions like slave or free translates to treating all colleagues with equal respect regardless of role or background easing team projects and meetings. Co workers might reference the faith that justifies to encourage one another during high pressure deadlines fostering an environment of encouragement over competition. The clothing with Christ invites professional attire in behavior such as patience in emails or fairness in evaluations. This scriptural lens helps navigate hierarchies with grace turning potential rivalries into alliances grounded in shared purpose.

Which Verses Can Spark Meaningful Conversations

Specific quotes stand out for use in daily talks including the line about scripture imprisoning all under sin to discuss collective struggles openly with a friend. The verse on no longer being subject to a disciplinarian can gently challenge rigid workplace policies in a constructive chat with a supervisor. Another powerful line notes there is no longer Jew or Greek inviting neighbors to explore cultural similarities during local events. For through faith you are all children of God in Christ Jesus serves as a quiet anchor in family reflections on belonging and purpose. The promise of being heirs according to the promise can inspire co workers facing uncertainty to focus on long term collaboration.

These elements together guide faithful Catholics toward interactions marked by unity and grace across every relationship. The breakdown of the reading reveals layers that apply directly to varied contexts without forcing uniformity. Readers gain tools to live out oneness in practical ways that honor the text's call to faith. Over time such habits strengthen communities and personal fulfillment alike.

Thank you for praying today with RCatholicPrayer your fellow pilgrim on the path of repentance and conversion.

A fellow penitent seeking God's grace,

🙏 @RCatholicPrayer

Literary Titan Publishes Author Interview With Laurie Thomas Vass About Her New Book About the Dangers to American Citizen Liberty of Unregulated Corporate AI.

Literary Titan Asks Vass to Describe How Concentrating AI Development Within Powerful Corporations and Centralized Institutions Threatens Individual Liberty.

Literary Titan, a professional service organization of editors, publishers and professors conducted an in-depth interview with Laurie Thomas Vass about her new book, Rebellion to Tyrants Is Obedience to God: Ending the Danger of the Corporate AI Surveillance Machine, Gabby Press, September 2026).

The full extended published interview is available at: https://t.co/Gef772bTLv

Literary Titan: Why do you see AI governance as fundamentally connected to questions of individual liberty and self-government?

Vass: We trace the 3000 year Western Civilization ethical framework of individual trust and fair dealing among citizens to the principles of liberty and self-government of George Mason and Thomas Jefferson.
The Western Civilization ethical basis of self-government, in a representative republic, is to treat other citizens as you would wish to be treated.
The strength of the individualist ethical framework is that it provides a pathway out of the current American political morass, and dangers of corporate self-volition AI, by re-creating the founding principles of trust and honest dealing among citizens, at the most local level of community.
We argue that the technology of AI is an amoral agent because it cannot choose between good and evil, but that the technology, under the control of immoral agents is dangerous to liberty.

Literary Titan: What is the New American Covenant of Liberty, and what commitments would participating citizens make to one another?

Vass: We describe 3 different covenants among citizens to treat each other honestly and fairly.
The first covenant is an economic covenant among citizens in each metro region to agree to cooperate and collaborate in creating regional economic growth that cannot be disrupted by corporate AI.
Like many other Western Civilization historical covenants, this economic covenant aims at creating beneficial social order for the citizens who live in the region.
The second covenant is more theological in its mission of directing citizens to use their Divine Spark to create God’s Kingdom on Earth, in their fair treatment of other citizens.
The third covenant is a political promise among citizens to use the democratic institutions of government to protect the freedoms and liberties of other citizens.

Literary Titan: If communities began adopting your decentralized economic model, what changes would you expect to see over the long term?

Vass: In our Chapter 10 (How Red State Citizens Build An Entrepreneurial Capitalist Economy in Their Community), we describe a new regional economic development business model that civic leaders and economic development professionals can use to direct economic benefits to the citizens who live in the region.
Over the long term, we expect to see greater rates of capital investment in new small technology ventures that have the potential to grow into large corporations.
The corporate model we have in mind is SAS Institute, in Cary, N. C., which started out as 4 N. C. State students and staff who created, what is now, the largest private corporation in the world.

The full interview is available at https://t.co/Gef772bTLv, along with the Literary Titan 5-Star Review of the book.

text:
You raise an interesting point, but I wonder whether we should distinguish between a bargaining tool and economic coercion, or what some might describe as political blackmail.

Negotiation normally involves both parties having something to offer and a genuine opportunity to reach a mutually acceptable agreement.

But when one country threatens or imposes financial penalties and then offers to remove them in return for concessions, how much genuine negotiation remains?

Consider India, penalised over its purchases of Russian oil, with Washington arguing that those purchases helped finance Putin's invasion of Ukraine.

Yet America is now facilitating Russian diesel exports when it suits its own economic interests.

And let's not forget Greenland.

In January, Trump threatened additional tariffs of 10%, subsequently rising to 25%, against Denmark, Britain and six other European countries over their opposition to his ambitions for Greenland.

Those threatened tariffs were subsequently withdrawn, but the underlying question remains.

What did a country's trade with America have to do with its refusal to surrender sovereignty over Greenland?

That was not an ordinary disagreement over trade balances or market access. Economic penalties were being threatened to secure concessions on territory and sovereignty.

There may be legitimate trade disagreements with India, just as America has legitimate national security interests in the Arctic. But neither automatically justifies using trade penalties to achieve unrelated political objectives.

I would hesitate to call this blackmail in the legal sense, but the distinction between negotiation and coercion deserves serious examination.

When economic penalties are threatened before meaningful discussions begin, and relief depends upon accepting another government's demands, are we witnessing genuine negotiation or an ultimatum dressed up as diplomacy?

My concern is that economic sanctions and tariffs should serve clearly defined, proportionate and transparent objectives, rather than become instruments of selective political pressure.

Otherwise, where does principled foreign policy end and transactional politics begin?

And perhaps more importantly, what happens to the sovereignty of smaller nations when their economic security becomes a bargaining chip?

🇩🇪 🇺🇲 🇷🇺 Alice Weidel celebrates Trump's Russian diesel deal. But how much fuel can Putin actually deliver?

Alice Weidel, co-leader of Germany's Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), has welcomed Donald Trump's agreement with Vladimir Putin to ease restrictions on Russian diesel exports, presenting it as an example of economic pragmatism that Germany should follow.

“That's how it's done!” Weidel declared, criticizing Chancellor Friedrich Merz for maintaining sanctions against Moscow and relying on expensive liquefied natural gas imports. She portrayed Trump's decision as an alternative to what she called Germany's policy of escalation.

But the numbers complicate that argument.

 @BrennpunktUA pointed out that the initial 300,000 tonnes of Russian diesel amount to approximately 2.25 million barrels. Against US diesel consumption of roughly 3.7–4 million barrels per day, that represents just 14 hours of demand.

The calculation is broadly correct. It demonstrates the limited scale of the initial shipment, although it does not capture the full agreement, which envisages up to 4.8 million tonnes of Russian diesel over subsequent deliveries.

Nor is it accurate to say financial markets ignored the announcement. Diesel futures fell by nearly 5%, according to Reuters, indicating that traders responded to the prospect of additional supply. Whether that reaction translates into sustained price reductions will depend on actual deliveries and broader market conditions.

There is another obstacle: Russia's damaged refining industry. Repeated Ukrainian long-range strikes have disrupted petroleum processing, reduced production of refined fuels and forced Moscow to impose restrictions on domestic fuel exports. The agreement's larger volumes therefore depend partly on Russia restoring industrial capacity while its refineries remain vulnerable to further attacks.

The political implications extend well beyond fuel prices.

Trump's administration has authorized a temporary relaxation of sanctions on Russian diesel without announcing a reciprocal Russian commitment to stop attacking Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has said he would support sanctions relief if it secured such a ceasefire, but criticized the agreement for providing Moscow with an economic concession before any corresponding de-escalation.

The Financial Times and Axios have also reported that American envoys pressured Kyiv to halt attacks on Russian refineries, with Ukrainian sources alleging that Washington raised the possibility of restricting intelligence sharing. An American official denied that an explicit threat was made.

For Weidel, the deal offers a political argument against Germany's sanctions policy. For energy markets, its lasting value remains uncertain. The initial shipment is small relative to American demand, larger deliveries face production constraints, and the diplomatic consequences may prove more significant than the immediate supply increase.

The central question is whether the agreement ultimately secures measurable Russian concessions or simply restores part of Moscow's access to international fuel markets while the war continues.

Mali weighs its options amid US and Russian overtures

https://t.co/5iG8XURwg9

♦️ Mali is navigating competing US and Russian interests, using Washington’s renewed diplomatic engagement and Moscow’s military presence to strengthen its position without committing exclusively to either power.

♦️ On 31 August, US lawmakers introduced the Mali Security Partnership and Counterterrorism Act, calling for a diplomatic strategy against al-Qaeda-linked JNIM, an assessment of its financing and a review of Russia’s growing regional influence.

♦️ Washington has gradually restored security cooperation with Bamako through counterterrorism talks, joint military exercises in February 2026 and a proposed arrangement exchanging US security assistance for access to Mali’s gold and lithium resources, although no agreement has been signed.

♦️ Russia remains Mali’s main military partner through Africa Corps, formerly Wagner, but suffered a setback in April 2026 when its forces withdrew from Kidal following attacks by jihadist fighters and Tuareg-led separatists.

♦️ Despite its military presence, Russia has struggled to turn its involvement into economic investment. A planned gold refinery near Bamako, designed to process 200 tonnes annually, remains stalled by financing uncertainties and a lack of confirmed progress.

♦️ US-Mali relations advanced in February when Washington lifted sanctions on three senior Malian officials, including Defence Minister Sadio Camara, amid intelligence-sharing discussions and efforts to secure the release of a kidnapped American missionary. Camara was killed in a car bombing two months later.

♦️ Neither Washington nor Moscow currently offers Mali a comprehensive partnership. Russia provides military support but limited investment, while the US pursues counterterrorism cooperation and mineral interests without a unified strategy, allowing Bamako to maintain relations with both powers.

text:
SATURDAY, OCTOBER 10 — COLLEGE FOOTBALL FREE PICKS

FREE PLAY — DUKE -6.5 over GEORGIA TECH — 3:30 ET

The difference between these teams extends well beyond their records. Undefeated Duke enters with a substantially stronger underlying efficiency profile, ranking 34th nationally in opponent-adjusted EPA per play compared with Georgia Tech at 122nd. That is an enormous performance gap, and the specific personnel matchup makes it even more significant.

Georgia Tech is allowing 189 rushing yards per game. Now the Yellow Jackets must contend with Duke running back Nate Sheppard, who is averaging 7.1 yards per carry and has already produced nine touchdowns in four games. Sheppard's ability to generate explosive runs and contribute as a receiver presents a particularly difficult assignment for an undermanned defense.

Georgia Tech's injury situation is concentrated in precisely the wrong area. Defensive linemen Jordan Walker, Noah Carter, AJ Hoffler and Shymeik Jones have been ruled out, along with defensive back Daiquan White. Several other defenders are questionable. When multiple players are missing from the same defensive position group, the consequences extend beyond individual talent. Depth deteriorates, substitutions become more difficult, and maintaining gap discipline becomes increasingly challenging as the game progresses.

Duke can exploit those weaknesses through sustained rushing production, manageable third downs and improved red-zone opportunities.

Georgia Tech has also struggled to capitalize on its own scoring opportunities, converting just seven of 15 red-zone trips into touchdowns. That inefficiency becomes especially costly against an opponent capable of controlling possession and generating consistent rushing yardage.

The primary concern is the weather. Heavy rain in Atlanta could reduce offensive efficiency and increase the importance of turnovers and field position. Georgia Tech also benefits from an extended preparation period, so the Yellow Jackets should not be dismissed simply because of their disappointing start.

Nevertheless, the overall efficiency disparity, Duke's rushing advantage and Georgia Tech's extensive defensive injuries create a compelling case for the favorite.

Our independent matchup assessment makes Duke approximately an eight-point favorite or better under normal conditions. Even after allowing for weather uncertainty, the available -6.5 offers a reasonable advantage.

FREE PLAY — UNDER 55.5 OLE MISS/VANDERBILT — 3:30 ET

This is a situation where the weather could fundamentally change the offensive expectations.

Ole Miss enters with one of the SEC's more dangerous passing attacks. Quarterback Trinidad Chambliss has thrown for 1,222 yards while completing 70.8% of his passes. Under ordinary conditions, that efficiency creates opportunities for explosive gains and quick scoring drives.

Saturday's conditions in Nashville are anything but ordinary.

The remnants of Hurricane Isaias are expected to bring persistent rain, sustained winds and gusts exceeding 30 mph. Forecasts indicate precipitation throughout much of the afternoon, with potentially more than an inch of rain over the course of the day.

Those conditions can directly affect the components that make an explosive passing offense dangerous. Deep throws become more difficult to execute accurately, receivers face tougher ball-tracking conditions, and wet footballs increase the challenge of clean exchanges and secure catches. Strong gusts can also affect punts and field-goal attempts, potentially reducing scoring efficiency even when offenses move the ball successfully.

The matchup adds another reason to question whether this game reaches the market's scoring expectation.

Vanderbilt is averaging 25.4 points per game, but the Commodores managed only 14 points against Georgia last week. The offense has demonstrated that it can move the football, yet sustaining that production against quality SEC opposition has been a different challenge.

Vanderbilt's tendency to commit penalties is another potential drive-killer. The Commodores are averaging nine penalties per game, ranking among the nation's most penalized teams. Negative plays become particularly damaging when adverse weather makes recovering long yardage through the air more difficult.

Ole Miss certainly possesses the talent to score despite the conditions. However, a high-scoring result becomes less likely if both teams are forced into more conservative play-calling, longer possessions and fewer explosive passing opportunities.

The independent weather-adjusted projection falls in the neighborhood of 50–52 points, assuming the forecasted wind and precipitation materialize.

At 55.5, there is meaningful separation between that expectation and the posted total. The UNDER offers the stronger value, particularly if sustained winds remain elevated approaching kickoff.

FREE PLAY — FRESNO STATE +7 over BOISE STATE — 10:30 ET

Boise State brings an impressive four-game winning streak into this conference matchup, and quarterback Maddux Madsen has been outstanding. Through five games, he has thrown 11 touchdown passes without an interception, demonstrating excellent decision-making and ball security.

But winning the game and covering a full touchdown on the road are two different propositions.

Fresno State enters 4-1 with a defense allowing approximately 16 points per game. The Bulldogs have demonstrated the ability to keep opponents from producing the sustained offensive success necessary to create comfortable margins.

The most important matchup involves Fresno State's rushing attack against Boise State's defensive front.

Fresno ranks 22nd nationally in rushing EPA, while Boise State has struggled badly in rushing EPA allowed and tackling efficiency. That creates a realistic opportunity for the home underdog to establish the running game, stay ahead of the chains and avoid placing excessive pressure on quarterback Jayden Mandal.

Effective rushing production also helps control possession. Against a quarterback as efficient as Madsen, limiting the number of Boise State possessions can be just as important as stopping individual drives.

Boise's offensive personnel situation adds another concern for the favorite. Several important contributors have been dealing with injuries, including questions surrounding the running back and receiving groups. Those absences could make the Broncos more dependent on Madsen to generate offense without the same supporting cast.

There is also relevant recent history. Fresno State has won three consecutive meetings, including last season's 30-7 victory in Boise. That result came after Madsen suffered an injury, so it should not be treated as proof that Fresno has an inherent advantage. It does, however, reinforce the importance of personnel and game circumstances in this rivalry.

The primary argument against Fresno is obvious: Madsen is playing exceptionally well, and Boise has the passing efficiency to punish a defense that allows too many manageable third-down situations.

Still, our independent matchup assessment makes Boise approximately a five-point favorite. That creates value with Fresno receiving a full touchdown at home.

The difference between +7 and +6.5 is meaningful, particularly in a game where a competitive, lower-scoring outcome is plausible.

Fresno does not need to outperform Boise in every category. The Bulldogs need to establish their rushing attack, limit explosive plays and force the Broncos to earn points through sustained drives.

That is a realistic formula for keeping this game within a touchdown.

text:
I’m so sorry you’re dealing with this, but I’m glad it wasn’t worse! ❤️ As a licensed Florida public adjuster, and a Floridian that has been through more storms than I’d like to count..  I’d like to offer a little advice that I hope helps you navigate the claims process.

First, document EVERYTHING, including damage that may not be immediately visible and your personal property. Also, be very mindful of how you describe your damage. Words like “flood” have specific meanings in the insurance industry and can affect if your damage gets covered or not. Don’t assume or speculate about what caused the damage or that it’s obvious. Simply describe what you observed and let the evidence establish the cause. Keep photos, videos, receipts, and records of all communications with your insurance company. But don’t share everything right away. Sometimes less is more. Also, remember that the insurance company’s initial estimate isn’t necessarily the final word. Damage WILL be overlooked, and you have the right to question their findings.

Most importantly, PLEASE be cautious of the contractors, restoration companies, and public adjusters who often flood storm-damaged communities after a hurricane. Unfortunately, disasters attract opportunists looking to take advantage of vulnerable homeowners. Never feel pressured to sign anything on the spot, especially contracts involving insurance proceeds, and always verify licenses, insurance, and credentials before allowing anyone to perform work or represent you.

There are plenty of reputable professionals out there, but there are also those who prey on people during their most difficult moments.

If you have any questions along the way, please feel free to reach out. I’m always happy to offer guidance, even if you don’t need my services. Wishing you and your family a smooth recovery! ❤️

text:
Francesca

《Francesca》是路易斯·B·马洛尼（Louise B. Maloney）于1927年创作的一幅油画，来自俄亥俄州克利夫兰的美国艺术家。马洛尼出生于19世纪80年代末，她的艺术生涯极具时代特色，体现了20世纪早期美国女性艺术家的探索与表达。

这幅作品尺寸为95厘米高、77.5厘米宽，采用油画布材质。整体画幅纵向展开，体现出艺术家对比例和构图的细腻把控。画面右下方有签名“Louise B. Maloney”，这是唯一明确的书写标识，确认了作品的创作者身份。画作目前收藏于美国绘画与雕塑部门，属于欣曼·B·赫尔巴特收藏。

虽然作品缺少公开描述和具体主题说明，但马洛尼作为曾在纽约、意大利罗马接受传统与现代绘画训练的画家，她的技法强调画面表面的美感，营造出一种古老而典雅的视觉体验。这种技法似乎在画面质感和色彩处理上都体现了她独特的匠心，与其长期在意大利安托科利的生活经历相关。

从构造上看，画布保持原状，没有迹象显示后续有过改动或装裱的明显信息。对观者而言，建议仔细观察画面细节处的笔触处理，特别是画面色彩层次的叠加和笔触流动，这反映了马洛尼对油画材质的掌控及艺术表达的专注。

《Francesca》的艺术价值不仅在于其画面的视觉享受，更体现在作为一件时代艺术作品，对20世纪初美国产妇女艺术家的身份与创作环境的窥探。她在早年通过克利夫兰艺术学校和纽约艺术学生联盟的学习，以及对欧洲艺术传统的吸收，形成了这幅作品独特的艺术语言。这是连接美国与欧洲艺术的文化桥梁，也是理解当时艺术家生活与精神世界的珍贵窗口。作品虽未详细说明人物身份或故事，但其艺术表现本身便是对“Francesca”这一形象的深情刻画。

总的来说，观赏此作，除了关注画面本身的艺术技法和视觉元素，也应结合马洛尼个人经历与时代背景，理解作品中潜藏的文化与艺术身份。作品留有一定开放性，邀请观众在细节中发现美、解读情感，成为20世纪美国妇女艺术贡献的一个生动见证。

"Francesca" is an oil painting created by Louise B. Maloney in 1927, an American artist from Cleveland, Ohio. Born in the late 1880s, Maloney's artistic career offers a window into early 20th-century American women artists’ pursuit of individual expression and technical finesse.

The painting measures 95 cm in height and 77.5 cm in width and is painted on canvas. Its vertical orientation highlights Maloney’s careful attention to proportion and composition. The artist’s signature appears in the lower right corner, reading “Louise B. Maloney,” confirming authorship. The artwork is part of the American Painting and Sculpture Department, within the Hinman B. Hurlbut Collection.

While there is no detailed description or explicit thematic explanation regarding the subject "Francesca," Maloney’s background is significant. She studied art formally in Cleveland and New York and later in Rome under Maurice Stern. Known for employing a painting technique that gives her works an antiquated appearance, Maloney focused primarily on the beauty of the surface itself. This approach likely enhances the painting’s texture and color layering, producing a refined and somewhat timeless aesthetic, possibly influenced by her extended time in Antocoli, Italy.

Structurally, the canvas remains in its original state with no documented alterations or later re-mountings. For viewers, it is recommended to closely examine the brushwork and the layering of colors. These elements showcase Maloney’s command of oil paint and her dedication to exploring textures, which enriches the visual experience.

Beyond its visual qualities, this painting holds value as a cultural and historical artifact. It represents the identity and creative environment of a 20th-century American woman artist. Maloney’s education at the Cleveland School of Art, her participation in the Art Students League of New York, and her European studies collectively shaped a distinctive artistic language bridging American and European artistic traditions.

Although the painting does not provide biographical details about the figure portrayed or a narrative context, the artistic expression itself invites reflection on the sitter’s identity and the artist’s perspective. "Francesca" can be appreciated as a personal and artistic homage, presented through technique and surface beauty rather than explicit storytelling.

In conclusion, appreciating this painting involves both observing its formal artistic qualities—the handling of oil paint, composition, and texture—and understanding it within the framework of Maloney’s biography and the broader cultural context of her time. The artwork retains an open-ended nature, prompting viewers to discover beauty and emotional depth in its details, and stands as a notable testament to the contributions of early 20th-century American women artists.

🇮🇳 KARUR VYSYA BANK: PROFIT SURGES 45% — A REGIONAL BANK TURNING INTO A COMPOUNDING MACHINE?

10 October 2026 | Latest market data
A private-sector bank growing profits faster than advances deserves attention. But after a sharp share-price rally, the real question is whether the valuation still offers upside.

📊 Q1 FY27: THE NUMBERS
• Net profit: ₹756 Cr | +44.9% YoY
• Net interest income: ₹1,423 Cr | +31.8% YoY
• Operating profit before provisions: ₹1,096 Cr | +36% YoY
• Net interest margin: 4.34% vs 3.86% a year earlier
• Advances: ₹1.05 lakh Cr | +17% YoY
• Deposits: ₹1.23 lakh Cr | +15% YoY
• Net NPA: 0.19%

💰 VALUE + GROWTH CHECK
Around ₹340 on 9 October, the stock had a market capitalisation of approximately ₹32,839 Cr and traded at roughly 12× trailing earnings.
Why bulls are watching:
• Profit growth is outpacing loan-book growth.
• Stronger net interest income is supporting earnings.
• Low net NPAs indicate contained recognised bad-loan stress.
• Advances and deposits are expanding at healthy double-digit rates.
⚠️ WHAT COULD BREAK THE THESIS?
• Gross NPA edged up to 0.74% from 0.66% year-on-year.
• Rising deposit costs could pressure future margins.
• The stock is near its 52-week high of ₹358.65.
• At roughly 2.2× book value, it is not automatically cheap just because its P/E is near 12×.
📅 NEXT CATALYST: Q2 FY27 RESULTS
The upcoming results will reveal whether loan growth, margins and asset quality remain strong. Watch deposit mobilisation, credit costs and fresh slippages—not just headline profit.
Bottomline: Karur Vysya Bank combines strong earnings momentum with improving profitability, but much of the easy valuation rerating may already have happened. The next leg depends on sustained earnings growth and disciplined asset quality. A quality-growth candidate to track—not a buy signal at any price.

The Israeli Emergency Bandage: A Battlefield Lifesaver

While Israeli innovations have shaped military doctrine and force structures, they have also had a direct impact on individual warfighters, as seen in battlefield medical advancements. The Emergency Bandage—a simple yet highly effective hemorrhage control dressing developed by an Israeli military medic—has saved countless American lives. First introduced in the 1990s, the bandage features a built-in pressure applicator that allows soldiers to treat severe wounds with one hand.

The US military adopted the Emergency Bandage in the early 2000s, particularly as it faced increasing casualties in Iraq and Afghanistan due to IEDs and small arms fire. It is now standard issue in the individual first aid kits of American soldiers, special operations forces, and first responders.

Armored Bulldozers: A Critical Urban Warfare Tool

The Israeli military’s adaptation of the D9 bulldozer into a heavily armored combat bulldozer offered a battlefield-tested model that directly influenced American operations in Iraq. In 2003, the US military procured 14 Israeli-armored D9s, developed by Israel’s military engineering corps, for use in combat zones like Iraq. While it remains uncertain where these specific units were deployed in Iraq, their acquisition illustrates the growing recognition of Israeli expertise in modifying heavy equipment for urban warfare. Some reports indicate that armored D9s were used in the Second Battle of Fallujah, possibly equipped with Israeli-designed armor kits that enabled US forces to breach barricades, demolish fortified positions, and reduce the risk to dismounted troops. In Israeli service, the D9 has been heavily employed in Gaza, where it has been used to clear booby-trapped buildings, uncover tunnel shafts, and breach barricades under fire—often while under threat from IEDs and anti-tank missiles. To further protect operators and sustain the platform’s urban utility, Israel developed a remote-controlled version of the bulldozer. This unmanned variant allows forces to conduct critical combat engineering tasks in high-risk zones without exposing soldiers to direct fire, demonstrating how the D9 continues to evolve as a life-saving tool on the modern battlefield.

Active Protection Systems: Trophy’s Battlefield Impact

Israeli advancements in force protection have dramatically increased the survivability of armored platforms in combat. The Trophy Active Protection System (APS) is one of the most significant Israeli contributions to armored warfare. Developed by Rafael Advanced Defense Systems, the Trophy APS provides a layered defense against incoming anti-tank guided missiles and rocket-propelled grenades (RPGs), automatically detecting, tracking, and intercepting threats before they reach the vehicle. First battle-tested by the Israel Defense Forces in 2011, the Trophy APS quickly proved its effectiveness in combat situations.

One of the greatest challenges in urban warfare is the vital need for mobile protected firepower—tanks and armored vehicles must operate in dense environments where threats lurk behind every corner and through every window. Traditionally, urban combat has exposed these vehicles to devastating RPG ambushes launched from concealed positions in buildings, alleyways, subterranean networks, and elevated vantage points like upper stories and rooftops—highlighting the multidimensional threat posed by the urban battlespace. The Trophy APS revolutionized urban warfare by reducing this vulnerability, allowing tanks to maneuver through the labyrinth of dense urban combat with far greater survivability. The system’s ability to neutralize RPG fire before impact has greatly contributed to the restored utility of heavy armor in close-quarters battle, a critical capability that modern militaries, including the United States, have sought to preserve.

Recognizing the increasing threat of modern anti-tank weapons, the US Army integrated the Trophy APS onto M1 Abrams main battle tanks beginning in 2018. By 2020, Trophy-equipped Abrams tanks had been deployed in Europe. Its ability to keep tanks in the fight by neutralizing anti-tank guided missiles has significantly influenced armored warfare for both nations.

Furthermore, as unmanned aerial threats evolve, the Trophy APS is now being adapted to counter drone-based attacks. Israeli defense developers are integrating drone-detection sensors and electronic countermeasures into the system, ensuring that armored vehicles are protected not only from ground-launched projectiles but also from loitering munitions and swarm drone attacks—a growing concern in modern battlefields, particularly in urban combat zones where drones are increasingly used for reconnaissance and precision strikes.

Countering IEDs

During the Iraq War, improvised explosive devices (IEDs) produced a majority of US casualties. They were so devastating that General John Abizaid, the commander of US Central Forces Command, asked for a “Manhattan project-like” effect to counter the threat in 2004. One of the first places the United States turned to for help was Israel. Having faced IED threats for years from Hamas, Hezbollah, and other terrorist organizations, Israel’s counter-IED capability far exceeded that of the United States. Israel shared these technologies with the United States, providing it with vehicle-mounted microwave devices called Dragon Spike and Dragon Spike II to test in Iraq and Yuma Proving Ground in Arizona. These devices were not a silver bullet to the IED problem, but they did help jump-start the United States’ counter-IED efforts.

Military Working Dogs: K9 Corps

Israel’s combat experience in dense urban areas has shaped its highly specialized use of dogs, and these operational lessons have increasingly informed US military practice. The IDF’s Oketz Unit began refining off-leash, with the handler using radios to pass commands beyond line of sight, canine tactics in the 1990s, where handlers faced environments too dangerous or constrained to accompany their dogs directly. In response, Oketz developed techniques to train dogs to operate independently—entering buildings, tunnels, or ambush-prone corridors to detect and neutralize threats without direct handler oversight. During operations in Iraq and Afghanistan, US forces began to adopt similar methods, sending dogs ahead to scout confined spaces and reduce risks to personnel. The IDF’s success using dogs to locate tunnel shafts, detonate traps, or even engage combatants contributed to a renewed appreciation within the US military for the life-saving potential of military working dogs in high-risk environments. Joint training exchanges, particularly among US Special Operations Forces and Israeli counterparts, have reinforced this bond, with Israeli doctrine and battlefield experience helping refine how American handlers prepare for modern urban combat.

Counter-Tunneling Technologies: Lessons from Israel’s Underground War

Israel has long faced the challenge of subterranean threats, particularly from Hamas and Hezbollah, which have developed extensive tunnel networks for smuggling, infiltration, and surprise attacks. In response, Israel has pioneered cutting-edge counter-tunneling technologies, integrating ground-penetrating radar, seismic sensors, AI-driven detection systems, and rapid tunnel-neutralization techniques. For almost a decade, the United States and Israel have collaborated on developing anti-tunnel technology to address these complex challenges. This partnership has led to the United States–Israel Anti-Tunnel Cooperation Enhancement Act, which authorizes $80 million annually—matched dollar for dollar by the Israeli government—to scale up essential anti-tunnel cooperation. This collaboration has directly influenced US border security strategies, particularly along the US–Mexico border, where drug cartels and human smugglers have constructed increasingly sophisticated underground passages.

By leveraging Israeli-developed sensors and detection methodologies—many tested and refined in high-threat environments like Gaza and Lebanon—US Customs and Border Protection has enhanced its ability to locate and dismantle these tunnels before they become operational. The enduring cooperation between the United States and Israel in countering subterranean threats underscores how battlefield-driven innovation can have broader applications beyond war zones, securing borders, protecting critical infrastructure, and denying adversaries the strategic advantage of underground warfare.

Targeting Pods and Precision Rockets: An Israeli-American Airpower Advantage

Originally developed by Israel’s Rafael Advanced Defense Systems and now co-produced with Northrop Grumman, the LITENING targeting podhas become a cornerstone of precision airstrike capability for the US Air Force. Designed for real-time target acquisition, tracking, and laser designation, the pod is now being used aboard F-16s in a novel role: enabling the use of laser-guided Hydra-70 rockets, upgraded through the Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System (APKWS). In current operationsagainst Houthi-launched one-way attack drones, US aircraft are pairing the LITENING targeting pod with APKWS to destroy drones at a fraction of the cost of traditional air-to-air missiles. Each APKWS shot costs approximately $35,000–$40,000, compared to the $400,000–$500,000 cost of an AIM-9 Sidewinder or the $1 million price tag of an AIM-120 Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile (MRAAM). This innovative pairing of Israeli-developed targeting systems with affordable US precision munitions reflects a growing shift toward cost-effective, scalable solutions for countering drone threats—challenges that have become a hallmark of modern airpower.

Israeli Enhancements to the F-35: Improving US Air Superiority

Israel has also played a crucial role in enhancing US airpower. The F-35 Lightning II, considered the most advanced stealth fighter globally, has benefited from Israeli-driven modifications that have expanded its capabilities. The Israeli Air Force was the first international operator of the aircraft, designating the F-35I the “Adir,” and quickly adapted the platform to its unique operational environment. Israel integrated enhanced electronic warfare systems, upgraded sensors, and domestically developed weapons, all of which have influenced broader F-35 advancements.

One of the most significant adaptations occurred when Israeli engineers, working with Lockheed Martin and the Pentagon’s F-35 Program, developed a new capability allowing the external carriage of large-diameter precision-guided munitions on the aircraft’s wings. Originally designed to carry munitions solely in its internal weapons bay to maintain stealth, the Adir is now the only F-35 in the world to have conducted operational strikes using externally carried munitions. This modification has increased the jet’s strike capacity, providing an advantage in sustained air campaigns while offering valuable lessons for the broader F-35 program.

Iron Beam: Addressing the Drone Threat

One of the greatest emerging threats on the battlefield is the widespread use of enemy drones, particularly in swarming attacks that overwhelm traditional air defense systems. In response, Israel has developed the Iron Beam, the world’s first high-energy laser air defense system. Developed by the Israeli defense technology company Rafael Advanced Defense Systems, the Iron Beam complements Israel’s existing Iron Dome air defense system with a cost-effective, near-limitless means of intercepting drones, rockets, and mortars. Unlike missile-based defense systems such as the Iron Dome, which require expensive interceptors, the Iron Beam neutralizes threats using laser energy. Expected to be fielded in Israel this year, the system has the potential to be a game-changer for defending critical military infrastructure and urban areas.

The United States has expressed strong interest in this technology as low-cost, high-volume drone attacks become a greater challenge. As the US military and its allies increasingly face drone swarm attacks, integrating laser-based defenses like the Iron Beam could provide a much-needed solution to this growing problem.

AI-Powered Warfare: The Future of Combat

Israeli artificial intelligence (AI)-driven innovations are reshaping modern warfare, influencing military advancements worldwide. The US military is also actively developing AI-driven technologies, sometimes leading the way and, at other times, drawing insights from Israeli advancements:

Harpy and Harop Loitering Munitions. Israel Aerospace Industries (IAI) developed these AI-enabled autonomous drones, capable of detecting and striking enemy targets without direct operator input. The US military has increasingly tested similar AI-powered loitering munitions for counter-radar and counter-vehicle applications.
Fire Weaver Battle Management System. Rafael’s Fire Weaver enables real-time target acquisition and optimized engagement using AI-powered coordination. The United States has experimented with similar sensor-to-shooter networks for improving battlefield situational awareness.
AI-Powered Counter-Drone Systems. Rafael’s Drone Dome is an AI-powered counter-drone system designed to detect, classify, and neutralize enemy drones. As drone threats from non-state actors continue to rise, the US military has adopted similar AI-driven counter-drone technologies to enhance the protection of bases and forward-operating units.
CARMEL AI Armored Vehicle. Israel’s CARMEL project integrates AI into armored fighting vehicles for semi-autonomous operations. The US Army’s Next-Generation Combat Vehicle program is evaluating AI-assisted technologies similar to those pioneered in the CARMEL project.
AI-Based Cyber Defense and Signals Intelligence. Israeli defense firms, many led by Unit 8200 veterans, have pioneered AI-enhanced cybersecurity and signals intelligence solutions. The US military and intelligence agencies have likely worked closely with Israeli firms to integrate AI-driven tools and predictive threat analysis into their operations.
These AI advancements underscore the broader evolution of Israeli defense technology, which continues to shape the future of warfare in partnership with the United States.

From kinetic defense systems like the Trophy APS and the Iron Dome to cutting-edge AI applications in battle management and cyber warfare, Israel’s military innovations have significantly enhanced US combat capabilities. The unique challenges faced by the Israeli Defense Forces—urban warfare, asymmetric threats, and high-tech adversaries—have led to significant advancements that align closely with the needs of US forces. Additionally, Israeli modifications to the F-35 and the development of the Iron Beam showcase how the US–Israeli defense partnership is not just about adoption but also co-evolution, advancing military technology to stay ahead of emerging threats.

As warfare evolves, the US–Israeli defense partnership will remain at the forefront of military innovation, ensuring both nations stay ahead of emerging threats and shape the battlefields of the future."

text:
The Real Harm of a Public Execution

09OCT2026
By Graeme Wood
The Atlantic Gift Article link
https://t.co/BTlOZsL8Mn 
It is hard to appreciate how awful this viewing experience will be, until you have it.

Yesterday, in an interview aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said the United States would soon carry out its first public execution since the 1930s. 

“We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it,” he said. Pentagon officials later confirmed that the execution will be livestreamed. 

The condemned man is former Major Nidal Hasan, who shouted “God is great” in Arabic before murdering 13 people at Fort Hood in 2009. Hegseth’s rationale for following this ancient practice is the same one offered by the ancients themselves: publicizing the agony of death and its unhygienic aftermath will remind onlookers that, in Hegseth’s words, there are “serious consequences” for treason. “No-brainer,” Hegseth said.

This pitiful creep—Hasan, I mean—deserves what he is probably going to get in December. 

The rest of us, however, will be ill-served by the spectacle of his execution. Many past criminals have had their head publicly cut off, or body nailed to a cross and left to rot there, as exemplary punishment. Such executions were once considered entertainment. Now the idea of recreationally watching a man be killed is so strange that few people understand what the experience will be like. Watching people die by violence, even if those people have it coming, damages the spectator irreversibly. I don’t mean physical or emotional damage, though many who see unnatural deaths up close do vomit and suffer from uneasy dreams afterward. Rather, I mean something more like the loss of their humanity and dignity, through partaking in the process of treating a person—in many ways so similar to themselves—like a machine to be turned off or ripped apart, a malfunctioning printer or an old car. To see this process is to be diminished, and the decision to make the execution visible to all is an invitation to self-harm, sent out to everyone with an internet connection. It is hard to appreciate how awful this viewing experience will be, until you have it. And then of course it will be too late. I have seen videotaped executions and have been diminished by every single one.

In August 2014, Hasan wrote a letter from prison to Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi, then the leader of the Islamic State, and asked to be granted citizenship as a “soldier of Allah.” No response was recorded. Ironically, it seems likely that Hasan would sympathize with Hegseth’s penchant for public execution, because the Islamic State interpreted the Quran to require that execution be carried out in public. Fornicators, according to Quran 24:2, should be flogged, and their punishment should be “witnessed” by a “group of believers.” By extension, the Islamic State determined, such a group should witness the punishment of all scripturally ordained crimes. Certain crimes, such as brigandage, are to be punished with crucifixion, an inherently public method of killing that the Islamic State carried out on video. Regrettably, I have seen footage of such a death.

From the July 2025 issue: Inside America’s death chambers
https://t.co/LY6qPPL37N

In the years before Hasan’s 2013 court-martial, he stopped shaving, in Islamic defiance of Army regulations that prohibit soldiers from growing beards. Mike Simpson, an Army officer and emergency-room doctor near the facility where Hasan was incarcerated, told me a few years later that he put the word out to colleagues that if Hasan ever had a medical emergency (not unlikely, given that he suffered paralysis and other conditions after being gunned down in the course of his terror attack), Simpson would like to be called to shave Hasan personally. The shaving would arise out of medical necessity—the patient might need a mask, with a reliable seal around the face—but Simpson, for his own pleasure, wanted to shear the bastard himself.
But the pleasure that might come from shaving Hasan would be quite different from what one might experience by shooting him in the heart. The Army won’t struggle to find a dozen willing soldiers to act as an execution party for Hasan. Hasan has said he wants death. Hegseth said he “doesn’t care” what Hasan’s final wishes might be. But I suspect that the volunteers’ enjoyment of their duty will be dampened if they notice signs of ecstasy from Hasan, as he is tied to a post 15 paces away from them and prays his way to the end. Hamlet could not bring himself to kill Claudius in prayer, because killing him in the midst of a holy act—“to take him in the purging of his soul, when he is fit and season’d for his passage”—would be too merciful.

In this world, denying Hasan the pleasure of death on his own terms, and letting him instead spend a few more earthly decades in tedious incarceration, would seem a much more onerous punishment. Therefore I would propose an alternative to public execution: public incarceration. Hasan should be placed in a small space, with a Pentagon-funded livestream of his remaining years. If the purpose of the spectacle of his death is to demonstrate to others the “serious consequences” of murdering 13 people, I doubt any execution would be more frightening than the slow, public aging of this repulsive murderer, as biology and time carry out his sentence. I would tune in to the livestream myself now and then, until I grew bored and found better things to do, and better ways to spend my own remaining time. This would take Hasan’s life and make from it a small gift to the rest of us, rather than taking something irrecoverable from us as we give martyrdom to him.

Graeme Wood is a staff writer at The Atlantic and the author of The Way of the Strangers: Encounters With the Islamic State.
