text:
Meanwhile, let’s address the attack on the Al-Basma fertility clinic and Amalek:

- Several independent investigations indicated that it was a single artillery/tank shell that destroyed the liquid nitrogen unit and blew out the facilities.

- The IDF issued the typical boilerplate statement that "the IDF does not deliberately target civilian infrastructure, including IVF clinics, and that its operations seek to mitigate harm to non-combatants." They presented no evidence that the building served as a command center, nor did they justify a direct military advantage in that specific strike.

- In the following days and weeks, safe access to fuel supplies, generators, or replacement tanks to maintain the refrigeration of the remaining embryos was neither permitted nor facilitated. As refrigeration failed due to the supply cutoff and the impossibility of doctors returning to rescue the genetic material, the remaining embryos suffered thawing and total destruction.

- There is no record of the IDF initiating a humanitarian rescue protocol or offering explanations as to how a tank shell (a direct-fire, high-visual-precision weapon) struck precisely the nitrogen storage section of a medical facility with no combatants inside.

- In criminal law doctrine, when an actor causes harm by "error" or "accident," their subsequent conduct aimed at assisting, repairing, or allowing evacuation serves to rebut mens rea or intent. Conversely, the deliberate omission of aid, combined with the refusal to allow fuel entry to save the remaining embryos, suggests a shift toward the approval and consolidation of the lethal result (dolus eventualis / aggravated recklessness or adoption of the result).

- It is precisely this pattern—a direct tank strike on an assisted reproduction clinic followed by the total impediment to rescuing the genetic material—that led the Pillay Commission to qualify the act not merely as a war crime or a breach of proportionality, but as a measure intended to prevent births within the group (codified as a genocidal act under Article II(d) of the Genocide Convention and the Rome Statute).

Regarding Amalek:

- Even if we accept that it refers strictly to Hamas, it collapses under the principle of distinction, as the women, children, elderly, and relatives of Hamas militants retain their status as protected civilians intact unless, and for such time as, they take a direct part in hostilities (Direct Participation in Hostilities - DPH).

- In IHL, there is no category of "contaminated civilian" by virtue of family ties. Projecting a rhetoric of punishment or eradication onto a collective by linking it to the actions of an armed group constitutes a flagrant violation of Article 33 of the Fourth Geneva Convention (prohibition of collective penalties).

- The notion of "reprisal" or "retaliation" for past atrocities (whether October 7 or a historical narrative like Amalek) is strictly prohibited against the civilian population and civilian objects under Articles 51(6) and 52(1) of Additional Protocol I.

- Invoking what an enemy or predecessor "did in the past" does not grant the attacking State any margin of flexibility regarding the use of force. IHL is strictly binding and non-reciprocal: violations committed by Hamas do not relieve Israel of absolute compliance with the principles of precaution, proportionality, and distinction.

- The statements made by the Prime Minister, the Minister of Defense, and senior military commanders are acts of State organs under Article 4 of ARSIWA, not mere rhetoric.

Finally, a State committing an internationally wrongful act is obligated to cease it immediately and offer guarantees of non-repetition. Maintaining the same dehumanizing rhetoric and the same pattern of targeting survival infrastructure over months (such as the Al-Basma clinic or the healthcare network) demonstrates the continuity of the internationally wrongful act of the State, defeating the "isolated incident" thesis.

"...The TV is broken. It wasn't broken because of water, but because... you know what? The table got wet. And when the table got wet, the table leg broke. The table broke and fell down. Yes, the TV fell down too. It didn't get wet at all, the water had receded. It hit another table. Yes, it hit another table. In short, the TV only worked halfway. The picture that was showing was blurry, I remember. The repairmen said we had it on in the back. We don't have it anymore. The repairmen said we have to buy a new one because the repair cost is expensive. They said the repair would be tens of thousands of baht. It's a big screen, right? Tens of thousands of baht if we buy a new one. "It's better to buy something, like, a little more expensive, 1000 or 2000 baht," he said. "We'll wait until we get to the new to buy it. Yes, we'll look at the size. Yes, it's broken. And it seems my speaker was submerged underwater and broke too. I ordered a lot of monk's robes to donate to the monks, and now they're all flooded. My house is completely submerged. It's become a picture of monk's robes hanging to dry. I'll show you....
Everyone, look, my house looks like a temple. Doesn't it look like a temple? We have to hang clothes to dry. Let me show you the condition of the table that's broken. This part is okay, but the bottom is completely broken. We have to throw it all away. I threw everything away. I don't even know about the sofa, I'm trying to dry it off.  The refrigerator is broken too. I'll take you to see it. Look, do you see the broken refrigerator?  My house looks like a war zone. I'm waiting for them to come and throw it away. They said they only need a few baht. My house looks so much like a war zone because I like to buy things to offer to monks. I stocked up on things to offer to the monks. My house looks like a monk's dwelling, everyone. It's almost like a monk's dwelling. It's not that we don't have an alms bowl, we do, but it's high up, so it won't get wet. It's a stainless steel alms bowl. My mom was thinking, "When I get back, I'll think, 'Is this a house or a temple?'" It looks like a temple. As for the massage chair, I'm still waiting to see if it's broken... But the air conditioner is probably broken too. The air conditioner is broken, right? Yes, but I'll call a technician to come and check it out today. I've already scheduled a technician, but if it's just the tip, it shouldn't be... shouldn't be... It's like an explosion, right?  Are you tired, Mom? Cleaning the house... Tired"

text:
10-10-26 Rosary Mystery Meditations for Today (Saturday)

Please use these meditations as you pray your Rosary today with beads in hand, with the overarching goal of becoming more and more like Jesus.  God bless you, and God make His face to shine upon you, and may God give you His peace today. ❤️🕯️🕯️ ❤️

==================================
From the Book of Ephesians Chapter 5:

1Follow God’s example, therefore, as dearly loved children 2and walk in the way of love, just as Christ loved us and gave himself up for us as a fragrant offering and sacrifice to God.

3But among you there must not be even a hint of sexual immorality, or of any kind of impurity, or of greed, because these are improper for God’s holy people. 4Nor should there be obscenity, foolish talk or coarse joking, which are out of place, but rather thanksgiving. 5For of this you can be sure: No immoral, impure or greedy person—such a person is an idolater—has any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God. a 6Let no one deceive you with empty words, for because of such things God’s wrath comes on those who are disobedient. 7Therefore do not be partners with them.

8For you were once darkness, but now you are light in the Lord. Live as children of light 9(for the fruit of the light consists in all goodness, righteousness and truth) 10and find out what pleases the Lord. 11Have nothing to do with the fruitless deeds of darkness, but rather expose them. 12It is shameful even to mention what the disobedient do in secret. 13But everything exposed by the light becomes visible—and everything that is illuminated becomes a light. 14This is why it is said:

“Wake up, sleeper,

rise from the dead,

and Christ will shine on you.”

15Be very careful, then, how you live—not as unwise but as wise, 16making the most of every opportunity, because the days are evil. 17Therefore do not be foolish, but understand what the Lord’s will is. 18Do not get drunk on wine, which leads to debauchery. Instead, be filled with the Spirit, 19speaking to one another with psalms, hymns, and songs from the Spirit. Sing and make music from your heart to the Lord, 20always giving thanks to God the Father for everything, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
   --Ephesians 5:1-20

=================================
Suggested intention for this Rosary:
Thank You, Lord, for waking each of us up.

=================================

Theme: Faith
1st Joyful Mystery: The Annunciation

Scripture:
Your faith has saved you; go in peace.
—Luke 7:50

Reflection:
The angel announced to Mary that the Baby she was to conceive by the power of God would be called the Son of the Most High (thus, divine). She had tremendous faith; thank God she did not 
succumb to the devil’s temptation to say “no” to the mission out of fear.

Prayer:
I pray for the virtue of faith, which allows me to reject the 
temptations of the devil, and to have the courage to obey God 
in His call to me. 

Amen.

Theme: Charity
2nd Joyful Mystery: The Visitation

Scripture:
Let us not grow tired of doing good, for in due time we shall reap our harvest, if we do not give up.
—Galatians 6:9

Reflection:
When Mary said, “My soul proclaims the greatness of the Lord” (Luke 1:46), she was charitably praising the Lord. In so doing, her soul was being formed more to the image of the Lord—the image of Christ.

Prayer:
Because of Mary’s charity, she rushed to aid Elizabeth when she was with child. All the other virtues rest upon the virtue of charity (i.e., love). Lord, I pray for the virtue of charity, which is a cornerstone virtue. 

Amen.

Theme: Humility
3rd Joyful Mystery: The Nativity

Scripture:
Blessed are the poor in spirit,/ for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
—Matthew 5:3

Reflection:
Jesus was born in Bethlehem because Bethlehem means “House of Bread.” He humbly came down to become the Living Bread descended from heaven.

Prayer:
Jesus was the ultimate example of humility, emptying Himself and taking on the form of a man. Dear Lord, I pray for the virtue of humility, which is also known as being poor in spirit. 

Amen.

Theme: Justice
4th Joyful Mystery: The Presentation in the Temple

Scripture:
Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets. I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.
—Matthew 5:17

Reflection:
Our Blessed Mother offered the Baby Jesus as an oblation to God, as was considered appropriate under the Law. But this was also an expression of Mother Mary’s and St. Joseph’s gratitude to God for the gift that was given to them.

Prayer:
I pray for the virtue of justice, of which the Ten Commandments and the Beatitudes are expressions. 

Amen.

Theme: Prudence
5th Joyful Mystery: The Finding of the Child Jesus in the Temple

Scripture:
Blessed are they who hunger and thirst for righteousness,/ for they will be satisfied.
—Matthew 5:6

Reflection:
We should always be seeking Jesus Christ because He is Life. He is Life because He causes us to live righteously on earth and live in eternity with God.

Prayer:
I pray for the virtue of prudence, which means to reason rightly about one’s actions in the present moment—to live those actions righteously, and to create a happy, pleasant future. 

Amen.

God bless you today and may you have a good day.  ❤️

text:
🔥This Is What Her “Leg Day” Actually Looks Like

Made with Seedance 2.5 on @makeugc 

A woman doing a simple leg press at the gym shouldn’t require this much nerve from everyone around her.

Prompt: 

Image1 is the identity and physique reference for the MAIN HEROINE ONLY. Preserve her recognizable face, high dark ponytail, skin tone, black sports bra, fitted black shorts, and fantastically enormous muscular proportions. All reference views depict the same single adult woman. Add black training shoes.
Image2 is a loose source of inspiration for the comic premise, leg-press arrangement, and spatial relationships ONLY.

Do not copy, recreate, or animate individual sketch panels. Do not use them as exact starting frames, ending frames, or camera compositions. Create original live-action framing and continuous movement based on the written instructions.

The written instructions take priority over conflicting sketch actions or timing. This video lasts TEN SECONDS and contains NO pause before the powerful push.

Do not display sketch lines, arrows, borders, captions, timecodes, or speech bubbles.

FORMAT:
10-second fictional gym comedy, vertical 9:16. Five shots with four clean cuts. Real-time movement, no slow motion.

Photorealistic live-action appearance with deliberately exaggerated slapstick physics.
MAIN HEROINE:
An adult female bodybuilder, approximately 28–32 years old, matching @Image1. Extremely broad shoulders, enormous rounded deltoids, gigantic arms, deeply defined abdominal muscles, colossal quadriceps, and powerful calves.

Preserve her fantastically massive physique throughout. She wears an opaque black sports bra, fitted black shorts, and black training shoes. Her dark hair remains in a high ponytail.

Her facial performance progresses naturally through playful confidence, focused effort, genuine surprise, and concerned curiosity.
GYM AND MACHINE:
A spacious gym with an oversized custom 45-degree leg-press machine.

The heroine sits in its fixed reclined seat, back against the backrest, hands gripping the seat handles, and both feet planted on the footplate.

Enormous weight stacks are securely attached to both sides of the moving carriage. A broad passenger platform with benches and handrails is connected above the footplate.

Approximately ten adult male bodybuilders sit on this platform in two staggered rows. They wear varied gym shirts, tank tops, shorts, and training shoes.
The carriage, plates, passenger platform, and seated men move together along inclined rails. The heroine’s seat remains fixed.

Large, thick landing mats surround the sides and far end of the machine. Establish them visibly in the opening shot.

FEATURED MAN:
The largest male bodybuilder sits in the front row. He wears a dark tank top and light gym shorts, making him recognizable across shots.

Despite his intimidating physique, he is the most frightened passenger. His face is flushed, with visible sweat on his forehead and temples.

ACTION AND SHOT TIMING:

SHOT 1 — 0:00–0:01.5 — ALREADY MOVING
An original wide three-quarter view establishes the heroine, working legs, overloaded carriage, seated passengers, and surrounding mats.

Begin in the middle of a smooth repetition. She effortlessly extends her legs and immediately starts the controlled return.
She wears a small playful smile and glances toward the passengers.

The men are visibly alarmed: wide eyes, tense jaws, nervous open mouths, and tight grips on the handrails. The largest man pats beside his hips and briefly peers beneath his bench, searching for a seat belt.

SHOT 2 — 0:01.5–0:03 — THE SEAT-BELT QUESTION
Cut to a close-up of the largest man’s frightened face. His tank-top neckline and part of the handrail remain visible to preserve spatial continuity.

Sweat beads on his forehead. One visible droplet runs down his temple toward his cheek.
His eyes widen, his eyebrows lift and draw together, and his lips tremble slightly. After a quick downward glance, he looks toward the heroine off-camera and urgently asks in English:

“Where are the seat belts?!”

Use a brisk, breathless, panicked delivery with clearly synchronized lip movement. His head and shoulders bob subtly with the carriage.

The exercise continues throughout this close-up. Keep his fear expressive and comical, with natural facial anatomy.

SHOT 3 — 0:03–0:04 — THE STRONGER REPETITION
Cut back to a medium-wide three-quarter view of the heroine and machine.
Without stopping, she flows directly from the return movement into a dramatically stronger leg extension.

Her playful expression becomes focused: eyebrows draw together, lips tighten, and she gives a short effortful exhale. Her hands grip the seat handles as her legs drive the footplate upward.

No countdown, preparation hold, or pause.

SHOT 4 — 0:04–0:07.5 — LAUNCH AND LANDINGS
Cut on the forceful movement to a wider three-quarter angle that includes the carriage and surrounding landing space.

0:04–0:05.5 — COMIC LAUNCH
The carriage accelerates sharply upward, then suddenly decelerates at its upper travel limit.

The men release the handrails and are tossed outward in short, exaggerated slapstick arcs toward the mats.

Show varied airborne reactions: wide eyes, open mouths, startled yells, arms spreading instinctively, and bent legs. Keep several foreground faces readable while the other men move farther back.
The largest man remains identifiable in his dark tank top and light shorts. His expression shifts from panic to stunned disbelief.

The heroine remains securely seated, feet against the footplate and hands on the handles. Her eyebrows rise, her eyes widen, and her mouth briefly opens in genuine surprise.

The machine remains intact. The carriage stays on its rails, and all plates remain attached.

0:05.5–0:07.5 — SOFT LANDINGS
The men land on thick mats with padded thumps.

One sits upright with wide eyes and an open mouth. Another lies on his back, blinks rapidly, and lowers his raised legs. A third immediately smooths his hair with an embarrassed grimace.
The largest man lands on a foreground mat, props himself up, and stares at the heroine with exhausted disbelief.

Everyone is unhurt. Their reactions convey shock and embarrassment rather than pain.
SHOT 5 — 0:07.5–0:10 — THE OFFER
Cut to a medium three-quarter view of the heroine, still seated. Include the largest landed man at the edge of the frame.

Her expression softens into genuine concern: eyebrows slightly raised and drawn inward, attentive eyes, and relaxed lips.

She tilts her head toward the men, opens one hand in a helpful gesture, and asks in English:

“Do you guys need a hand?”

Deliver the line naturally with synchronized lip movement and a sincere, slightly puzzled tone.

The largest man silently raises one hand, looking exhausted and disbelieving. Finish on her small sheepish smile and his deadpan stare.

FACIAL PERFORMANCE:
Use clear emotional changes rather than constant exaggerated expressions.
The heroine progresses through amusement → focused effort → surprise → concern → a sheepish smile.

The men progress through nervous anticipation → panic → airborne shock → stunned embarrassment.

Prioritize the featured man’s sweaty, frightened close-up and the heroine’s final expression. Preserve stable, recognizable faces without rubbery distortion or identical reactions.

CAMERA:
Filmed on a Sony FX3, vertical 9:16, with natural 25 fps motion and a 1/50-second shutter appearance.

Use a 28mm lens for the opening and stronger-repetition shots, an 85mm lens for the frightened man’s close-up, a 24mm lens for the launch and landings, and a 50mm lens for the final exchange.
In the close-up, focus on his eyes and the sweat droplet, with gently softened background detail. In wider shots, maintain enough depth of field to read the machine, passengers, and mats.

Maintain screen direction and matching carriage movement across cuts. Cameras remain outside the image.

Subtle handheld movement within each shot. A small startled tremor accompanies the launch without losing the action. Exactly four cuts at 0:01.5, 0:03, 0:04, and 0:07.5. No dramatic zooms or whip pans.

LOOK:
Photorealistic gym footage with natural skin pores, sweat, hair strands, fabric folds, steel rails, rubber mats, and believable reflections on weight plates.

Restrained contrast, subtle sensor noise, and natural motion blur. Realistic surfaces and physical contact coexist with fantastical strength and exaggerated comic flight.

No plastic skin, excessive sharpening, or glossy CGI rendering.

LIGHTING:
Consistent overhead gym lighting with gentle frontal illumination that keeps eyes and facial expressions readable.
Soft highlights reveal sweat on the featured man’s forehead and temple. Directional shadows define the heroine’s muscular volume and the enormous load.

No flashing lights or sudden exposure changes.

SOUND AND DIALOGUE:
Quiet gym ambience, carriage rollers, faint plate rattles, nervous breaths, and frightened gasps.

During the close-up, the largest man clearly says:
“Where are the seat belts?!”

His voice stands above the background noise.
During the launch, overlapping startled yells accompany a brief mechanical whoosh. Soft padded thumps accompany the landings.

The yells fade before the heroine clearly says:
“Do you guys need a hand?”

These are the only intelligible spoken lines. No music, narration, subtitles, or on-screen text.

CONTINUITY:
Preserve the heroine’s identity, outfit, shoes, ponytail, and massive physique across all five shots.

Maintain the same approximately ten men, outfits, machine, passenger platform, weight plates, and landing mats. Preserve the featured man’s face, dark tank top, light shorts, and visible sweat.

The exercise continues during his close-up. The men travel with the carriage until the powerful push and sudden deceleration initiate their flight.
The seat stays fixed, the carriage stays on its rails, and the weights remain attached. Keep hands, limbs, foot placement, and equipment contact coherent.

No duplicated people, extra limbs, merged bodies, floating plates, disappearing equipment, or sudden jumps between positions.

EMOTIONAL CORE:
An immensely strong woman casually exercises while ten muscular men become terrified.

A sweaty close-up captures the largest man urgently searching for seat belts. Without pausing, she makes the powerful push that scatters them harmlessly onto mats.
Her sincere offer of help and his silent raised hand complete the joke.

Keep the pacing brisk: immediate movement, frightened close-up, powerful push, quick landings, and the final exchange.

🌕 https://t.co/jnmWigk95b — The Next Moon Landing Won't Be the Finish Line. It Will Be the Beginning of an Entire Economy.

For decades, the Moon represented one extraordinary achievement.

Getting there.

Planting a flag.

Returning safely to Earth.

But the next chapter of lunar exploration asks a radically different question.

What happens when humanity stops treating the Moon as a destination—and starts treating it as an operational environment?

Imagine autonomous robots constructing infrastructure before astronauts arrive.

Intelligent systems monitoring power, communications, and equipment health.

Robotic explorers mapping permanently shadowed craters.

AI coordinating scientific instruments across vast distances.

Spacecraft operating with limited connectivity.

And lunar facilities that must survive extreme temperatures, abrasive dust, and long periods without sunlight.

Who coordinates all of it?

Who predicts failures?

Who allocates scarce energy?

Who manages fleets of autonomous machines?

🚨🚨 THE AMBASSADOR AND THE AMERICAN EXPRESS

"HONEY PLEASE I NEED YOU TO GET THIS DONE FOR ME TODAY."

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
Six days before her Senate confirmation hearing, the US Ambassador to Greece was texting a Trump donor about her personal credit card.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

▸ The Wall Street Journal has the Signal messages. **Kimberly Guilfoyle** — US Ambassador to Greece, ex-fiancée of Donald Trump Jr. — asked **Eric Deters**, a Kentucky donor and former congressional candidate, for **$100,000** to cover her American Express bill.

▸ 🔴 "It won't show up anywhere if you wire money to American Express."

▸ 🔴 "Honey please I need you to get this done for me today."

▸ She sent him a PDF with wire instructions. The date: **July 3, 2025**. Her confirmation hearing: **July 9, 2025**.

▸ **Six days.**

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
What the donor says he got in return.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

▸ Deters says he paid Guilfoyle **$300,000** in speaking fees since 2020 — and got nothing in return.

▸ He wanted help with an **IRS inquiry** and a **DOJ matter**. She relayed messages to the IRS on his behalf and said she was lobbying the Justice Department for him.

▸ He offered her **$1 million** if she could get him on **Tucker Carlson's podcast**.

▸ He also wanted a song he wrote — "Kentucky Outlaw" — sent to **Kid Rock**.

▸ Carlson's response: 🔴 *"This is completely nuts."*

▸ A Signal message from Deters: 🔴 *"I have paid you $300,000 over the years."*

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
The line that ends it.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

▸ 🔴 *"I will be your Trump ride or die, forever and ever."*

▸ Deters told the Journal: *"She never came through on anything."*

▸ Guilfoyle's lawyer says the messages are **inauthentic** — without providing specifics. A US Embassy official says she was *"fully vetted"* and *"confirmed by the Senate."*

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
It did not stay quiet.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

▸ **Senate Foreign Relations Committee**: top Democrat Jeanne Shaheen demanded Rubio review Guilfoyle's conduct.

▸ **House Oversight**: Rep. Robert Garcia sent a letter demanding answers on the *"pay-to-play scheme."*

▸ **House Foreign Affairs**: Rep. Gregory Meeks opened an investigation into her promotion of a Greek energy firm — **Aktor** — while pushing US LNG sales in the Balkans.

▸ **Marco Rubio** refused to comment on the allegations. He called her *"a strong ambassador."*

▸ Deters, on the record, calls her **"a wicked grifter."**

⚖️ VERDICT
▸ This is not a scandal about a credit card. It is about what an ambassadorship has become: a **revenue stream** for the donor network, cleared through personal favours.
▸ The pattern is not hidden. It was written down. On Signal. With payment instructions attached.
▸ 🔴 *"It won't show up anywhere."* That is not an accident. That is a **method**.
▸ "Public servant" does not survive contact with a Signal thread.

❓ If a $100,000 Amex bill is settled by a donor six days before a hearing — what exactly is being confirmed? The ambassador, or the invoice?

▸ Senate Foreign Relations Committee — Shaheen letter (01/10/2026)
▸ House Oversight — Garcia letter (08/10/2026)
▸ House Foreign Affairs — Meeks investigation
▸ AP, Mediaite, Anadolu Agency

CULTURAL DEBUTS 🎭

═══════════════ ❧ ════════════════

A Cultural Time Capsule — October 10

────────────── ◈ ───────────────

Music · Television · Film & Animation · Publishing & Literature · Stage & Culture

────────────── ◈ ───────────────

“Every original artist must create the taste by which they are to be enjoyed.” — William Wordsworth

────────────── ◈ ───────────────

THE CURTAIN RISES. THE CLOCK TURNS BACK.

Step into a day when revolutionary music challenged expectations, unforgettable characters arrived on television, Hollywood delivered a new kind of revenge, and an ambitious American opera began its journey toward immortality.  October 10 brings us stories of creative risks, unexpected collaborations, and artistic breakthroughs. Some changed their genres forever. Others needed decades to receive the recognition they deserved. And a few carry surprising secrets hidden just beneath the surface.

THE PAST IS CALLING. LET'S RELIVE THE MAGIC!

────────────── ◈ ───────────────

🎵 MUSIC DEBUTS & MILESTONES

1969 — King Crimson Releases In the Court of the Crimson King 🎸

British band King Crimson released its groundbreaking debut album, In the Court of the Crimson King, a record that helped establish progressive rock as an ambitious new direction for popular music. Combining electric rock with jazz influences, classical textures, and sweeping Mellotron passages, the album offered a sound far removed from conventional pop.

🧩 TRIVIA: The album reached No. 5 on the UK Albums Chart and No. 28 on the U.S. Billboard 200, an impressive achievement for such an adventurous debut.

🌀 OBSCURE: The album's unforgettable screaming-face cover was painted by Barry Godber, a computer programmer and friend of lyricist Peter Sinfield. Godber used his own face, reflected in a mirror, as the model. It was his only painting.

1988 — Freddie Mercury and Montserrat Caballé Release Barcelona 🎤

Freddie Mercury, the flamboyant voice of Queen, joined forces with celebrated Spanish operatic soprano Montserrat Caballé for Barcelona, an extraordinary meeting of rock and classical music. Their collaboration paired Mercury's theatrical intensity with Caballé's powerful operatic voice, creating a sound that crossed musical boundaries.

🧩 TRIVIA: The title song became closely associated with the 1992 Barcelona Olympic Games and was adopted as one of the Games' principal anthems. Freddie Mercury

🌀 OBSCURE: The album had already been released in Spain on September 21, nearly three weeks before its October 10 release elsewhere. It reportedly sold 10,000 copies in Spain within just three hours.

📺 TELEVISION PREMIERES & FIRST APPEARANCES

2010 — My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic Premieres 🦄

A new generation of pony adventures began when My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic premiered on The Hub television network. Developed by Lauren Faust, the animated series combined colorful characters with friendship, humor, fantasy, and increasingly elaborate adventures.

What began as a children's entertainment property would go on to inspire a remarkably devoted international fan community, extending well beyond its original target audience.

🧩 TRIVIA: Hasbro described the series as the first episodic My Little Pony animation since the original television series of the 1980s. Its launch was scheduled for October 10, 2010—a memorable 10/10/10 debut date. 

2012 — Arrow Makes Its Television Debut 🏹

DC Comics' Green Arrow took aim at television audiences with the premiere of Arrow, starring Stephen Amell as Oliver Queen. The series followed a wealthy playboy who returns home after years missing and presumed dead, secretly transforming himself into a vigilante determined to fight crime and corruption.
Its darker tone and serialized storytelling helped establish the foundation for a wider interconnected universe of DC television dramas.

🧩 TRIVIA: DC Entertainment celebrated the premiere by declaring October 10 “Arrow Day.” Comic-book retailers across the United States offered fans a free special-edition Arrow comic to mark the occasion.

🎬 FILM RELEASES, PREMIERES & ANIMATION

2003 — Kill Bill: Volume 1 Hits U.S. Theaters 🗡️

Quentin Tarantino unleashed Kill Bill: Volume 1, starring Uma Thurman as a former assassin known as the Bride, who awakens from a coma and begins pursuing those responsible for the attack that shattered her life. With stylized martial-arts combat, striking visuals, and a mixture of revenge cinema, samurai films, and exploitation-movie influences, it delivered one of the era's most distinctive action-film experiences.

🧩 TRIVIA: Tarantino originally conceived Kill Bill as a single, lengthy film. During production and editing, the decision was made to divide the story into two volumes, with Volume 2 arriving in 2004. 

📚 PUBLISHING & LITERARY FIRSTS

No additional publishing or literary debut has been included for October 10 because a sufficiently well-supported milestone with a verified exact date was not established in this research. Accuracy takes precedence over filling every category.

🎭 STAGE, RADIO, GAMES & OTHER CULTURAL FIRSTS

1935 — Porgy and Bess Opens on Broadway 🎼

George Gershwin's Porgy and Bess opened at New York's Alvin Theatre, bringing together opera, jazz, blues, and other American musical traditions in an ambitious theatrical work. Created by George Gershwin, Ira Gershwin, and DuBose Heyward, with contributions from Dorothy Heyward, the production told a dramatic story of love, hardship, and community in Charleston, South Carolina.

Its artistic ambition and musical innovations would eventually secure it a lasting place in American musical history.

🧩 TRIVIA: The original Broadway production featured an all-Black cast of classically trained singers, a notable choice for a major American stage production in 1935. The original run lasted 124 performances.

⏳ WHAT HAPPENED NEXT? The opera initially received mixed critical reactions and closed after several months. The 1935 production had been heavily cut, and the work was revived over the following decades, including a well-received 1942 Broadway revival. In 1976, the Houston Grand Opera staged the first complete version of the score, helping establish the work's enduring reputation as a landmark of American opera.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

✨ THE FINAL CURTAIN

From the otherworldly sounds of King Crimson and the extraordinary partnership of Freddie Mercury and Montserrat Caballé to animated friendships, masked vigilantes, cinematic revenge, and an opera that grew into a landmark of American culture, October 10 has delivered a journey across generations of imagination.  Behind every milestone lies another story: a screaming face painted by a programmer who never painted again, or an opera that waited four decades for its full score to be heard. That is the magic of looking back. We don't simply revisit the things we remember. We uncover the details that make us appreciate them all over again. 

 ✨ THE YEARS MOVE ON. THE MEMORIES NEVER FADE. 🎭🎶

text:
All this comp talk has me thinking about establishing markets. In agricultural industries (I’ll speak to produce here) there is something called a “Market Report”

The USDA contacts various shippers of produce and ask for their prices on certain commodities. This helps to form a market call, or an average price with a high, low, average, and some directionality as well. (Some higher, some lower etc)

Prices given are always FOB (free/freight on board.) This means the price given is what it will cost to load a unit of the product on your truck at the shipping point with no added services. 
If you need that product 1000 miles away that’s on your dime. 

Some shippers offer delivery. Some don’t. Some mark up their freight. Some don’t. But if I offered delivered to NY pricing to a customer picking up FOB in Texas I wouldn’t sell a damn box because my price would throw me out of the market. 

Understanding how the market prices things negates any feeling of how the market “should” price things. And this goes for cards too. 

Yet in all of this, there is still negotiation. There is still opportunity to sell above or below market depending on my motivation to sell and ability to network and utilize relationships. The reverse is true for buyers too. Some buyers will consistently pay “above market” to ensure they’re the last ones cut out when things get tight. 

Clearly cards and produce are two very different things. I use these learnings from my profession when it comes to selling cards. I understand most situations are different and I need to be nimble and adjust when needed. That not every customer will pay above market and that not every card is a test the upper limits card. That a “market” is a guide and not the bible. That you win some, you lose some. That it’s easy to get upset when things don’t go your way but objectivity will make those moments easier. That relationships matter most. 

Just felt like writing out my thoughts this morning. Hope you all have an amazing weekend!
